## Broken Pump Raises Toxic Plume Concerns
A [broken pump](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAUxvGn0Q7DQUQpKLaxm223NCweBhIUAsfx3re_mXmFW3_JP_l9_x7bw8YUz-dfe6ChHPx24t0SEmHdKH9FV9J1oEdbm7f2WfN17m0TXCgGwEBupeZW0NEG_W4kjuB1jwZmLdUk9Sz7YPgywSSXRWsnR-s8ggCtPaKyQnC39NG8gwAgAUDBOCwKdyXnWdoJF_yvOslxj5TrQAFziNmn7_zCOrh89MkEotK68U8n1k6s930PNqf31onVVoouYevEWq6jMG9juioyChUt4dnYh8k-TiYAuBw550OgI_XV7OWOKcWm5k7y52Hjp9vTr896GfETAAD__55GgA8) at Chillicothe’s U.S. Paper Mill could allow a toxic underground plume to spread toward nearby homes, farmland, and the Scioto River, the company warned. The mill notified the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency that the decades-old, 90-foot pump had fractured and [needs to be replaced](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb_G3oj8MAF7YOjiLV07Ws_4EVDBICBJ-_eV8wud79XRPffrtt7QB3_cPzGSbsnZ9aBXDdQalbWlH29yeESyhKVaxHtJj2OvKx-4ZAAMxJpLqplMW6HftaAR7NyTBjULeRWzEr3T84azBC45KmsU8EnZCXAgEoqkkmPv9QkEAAEAEsbLJGmXQimBV5pok50YaPctlUtzlJxPNvymJ5WLSbEP2rWWazd-dHzp-HIa2FQMcaHOQseXraRvOlh-xMwK-kqVYcAS2Qlhb0_2FmUbHYTNMeN8CN6k5ohFHwJ7YTlqx5e-6D2_zrBK1YnhHtGH94727wOfmv8FAAD__7kdiOo), at a cost of thousands of dollars. The contamination [originated at the WearEver Aluminum factory](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkL1yrCAUx58GO3eEZVEKitvY7W1TOkc4CDMoDJxdk7fPmDxC-t__8-O5PCGmeGz_YUdDOfjlwLMlJMK6UP6MtqTXjh6hNg-w1fw6XFvEIFTPec_lUmpuBS0tvHNG4p173aHho5bqIfUou2BW1Ah-UpMYwLqHnFYUcvVyQqfXVegumsuQcy4554rfb5NCp-Q4SnjghKtickAXKdcbBcwhZp--8hvrzea9SyYQlcbu_5iYmZjP87ywkhsBBTzaRTExQ6VoEzIxX2lMzINmYrYhphRtpoB9gYK132NKvc0HwR4PIHT97-wTCGtXjSvnJWlqZHLYdojppwb9-b-3Ed8BAAD__-Q1iOI), which operated from 1948 until the late 1990s and left trichloroethylene, lead, and cadmium in the soil and groundwater. A mill official called the failure a “potentially urgent situation” but said that residents didn’t need to worry about their water at this moment. The replacement timeline remains unclear.

## FAA Lifts Nationwide Ground Stop
The FAA said flights could resume Friday night after lifting a nationwide ground stop that halted every departure in the country for hours, the first since 2023 and only the second since 9/11. [Live updates here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFygzAMBuCngc05WzgmDB66sKVrR05gAeo5mDMKub59z-kjdJZO-r__6z7ckSNvyyc-yMucho1eRyQRysOS03MLh6Q98iwUMp-Ux4QygAanjFHGDjgJnzSYOviZCKipyZu2s-7q9O1Wr74dOzNeXYPgaB41hRbg5gCc1leydqrZl3PGGGtMY6270NTZrkVtTWNb1G1lNQWWlC_fiTdZaY4_6aR8mdKjjn4V2Y-q-aigr6DHvQjKqII-8kkV9H8QVSQKT0bhtKk58rLKocq6eu4BhY63qVElT5192F8cIx-uJFgeyPH9Uf7X0-nhNwAA__9MiHyD). A communications outage hit the 22 regional centers that guide planes between airports. Some 3,500 planes in the air were allowed to land, but nothing took off. Europe suspended U.S.-bound departures, Mexico grounded northbound flights, and some 11,000 flights carrying [1.5 million passengers](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhTAQRE9jOhBr_G0oXKSh-2lTosVefxwZjMwGlNtHJEdIM81Ib_Tm4zk9Maa4vd5xJcshTxtdRyJmKtOr5K_NH5z3FAOTL_GkMmfkSbZS1wA1qAkdx5MmqLwNRJK6iiyYQemHbvu-Wqw2s3tg30uj_DAH541_KBmIUMu-H7CK9sYBgALolNINuUENBlsFnTLYGqFa8pFzaT5z3HihkL7zSaVxea2SXZj3Q3RvQo5Cjtd1NW6b3V0KOd5oIUeAOzohx4BY_4nVt1mz8JqqYv1-xZTioe-114ox_dL5f5-cVv4EAAD__5eOdIY) were scheduled to depart after 4 p.m. ET. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said new technology layered onto the FAA's aging analog system overwhelmed it, and that there was "no indication" of a cyberattack. Sources separately blamed a [botched software update](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O4zAMhU8jdwpMSf4rVGzjLttuadARnXChSIbMOMjtB5o5wjRsSHx83_t3Xa7IkdP9Lz7Jy5aXRO8jkgiV5V7yK4VD8h55EwqFTyprRllMa3oNoMEteBM-aYEm-I3IkG3IwzC5vuvbcWwefhwQpym0uFLX4jqZbug211sYQ7daOzTsKw4AHIB1rr_QbXLTgK0D6wZsB-VaCiy5XP5nTvKgLX7ySeVyy88m-ofIfij7R5lZmTl99nxIXSkzV7AyM0AdVpn5degqqMy8IeqEwjm9OZD-cdVVVkc-Sb_2gEL1sik-7G-OkY--Zrk_keP3b_ldY6c3XwEAAP__YQJ-7w). Microsoft said its outage was unrelated. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed "overloaded" routers, called the situation "an emergency," and asked Congress for billions more to [overhaul air traffic control](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2vnTAMQH9N2HKVryYwZOjC9rp2RIY4kDY3QcEPdP99RXuH7m_1ka1z_PNj-oCUU1l_wBM9xToVvI6MRNimtdXPEg6qe06RMLR0Ypsr0KSEslxKLs0EC6UTJ9kFHxEV6g69dIOx36zo-27zdug1WmnB2F66eYjaGmcCDCoEEWfXJX-fk1IaKbUx9oHLYAYHwkhtHAjHjMCQqLbHr5oKbRjzq57YHkt9dtlvRPvB9HemRqZGmBd3N9yQqTGnE_nnHoDwYGqMAPxfFr-7-P-YXxsQ_13qxQtQquVKAXnMad3o4NDwvYmBqVEJofu-d0yNWKi93qNBaM3U2DUf9ivlnA57669PSPmvLn3tyadXfwIAAP__UwGQ7A). Nearly 5,000 flights were canceled during the four-hour stop, and Duffy said the FAA would prioritize getting stranded college football teams to today's games.
## Tanker Capsizes Riverboat in New Orleans
A 520-foot asphalt tanker lost control and [T-boned a docked riverboat](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAQQL_G7rBgTMAuKK5xl2uvtAgMCbcEIhjbyt-vHO0fbPekGY3em3_X9Wpjivn-1z7RUChrxqMlJMK63mvZsm9UXikGQl_jjvVWLK3AQTEhmJCrdRR3XEXvTUAEHHs0Qs9SXRSfpv5hBPeT1hc-S5CIANojwGy1UiFImEIfzXlOCCGFGKVUA7pZztpyKUapLded5OgjlTr8LzHTA0N6lx3r4MqzT-ZB9Grd-KeDpYPlOI4h39yZcc47WE7sYNka-6GKzW3ItuyxHvbNSkyMbP7CylxJKXr8rLJSE9rc2KebneGsumwVn2G89NX41xFTik2dhvenjeljRL_7427gOwAA__8Zdokc) on the Mississippi River near the French Quarter on Friday, flipping the paddlewheeler _American Heritage_ with about 129 passengers aboard and sending people into the water. All passengers and crew were accounted for, and 32 were hospitalized with non-critical injuries. New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno called it "a miracle on the Mississippi." Video showed people in [life jackets](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unTAQhJ_GdD7yLuavcJGG7qZNiXzxAs4xNrIX0Hn7iLzCbaYZ6dM38-dr-rI--Lj-tjsZXtIU6S6BmClPa05ndIXTEfzC5LK_KH8nyxMqbCWABD3Zmf1FE1TOLERIdUUGukG3Tav6vtpMXyM6p9Q3Yg9AznVWN27ooFELDQ4qbx4cAGiAWuv2RfOgh84qDbXurOqEVuQ8p_z6m3zkjZbwSRfl15z2KpiN-Sii_iVwFDjGz5EKP5XA8QELHAGeqAWOZ5HPQIEj2_imLDfPRbo0v8nJOZ--kCybP-TteZN7yiR5s1ECNvKwpVBcKReZqcwnFXlGR_m2H4FjlY07bh-CL-1jvO7Wh_-G_LNfL4P_AgAA__9DTYzV) clinging to the capsized hull and life rings in the river. The riverboat had docked about two hours earlier to begin letting passengers off after an eight-day cruise on the Mississippi River. The Marshall Islands-flagged tanker _Atlantic Asphalt_ had [arrived in port](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAURb_G7hgBJmZcUKRxt2lTWs_wbL8MBgRvPUq-PvL-wkq3u9LVuef3x_IBFCntv-BEx1teEr5bRGasy17zZwqNc4m0MYZKF9Y1Ay9a6lEoJZRZwDNduKg-uA1R49CjU3Yy449RPp_94QavbRie02rBbts4Kqm8H-QEVkuv1rUnd88ppYxSgzHjA_1kJgvSqMFYkLYzEgNxro8_mRIfuMW_-cL68PnsozuYS-uGn52eOz3vHgoDpbvs9MyQXlhF40ovbCJk_8IgCoQQ8X0gRqwiJ3FSa3dKIfF1U3j4bJR2QSw4Cw-l0T_s9NxXF8qbYqQ23mT7CRS_SPh7_i6n_wcAAP__CcCIAw) two days earlier. The Coast Guard and NTSB are investigating, though their teams were delayed in getting to the city by the nationwide ground stop. Nobody is trying to repeal the Electoral College anymore. Repeal would take a constitutional amendment -- two-thirds of Congress, then 38 states. Dead on arrival, and both sides know it. Instead, the plan is simpler and entirely legal: don't change the Constitution. Change the electors.
**The mechanism**
The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (**NPVIC**) is an agreement among states. Every signatory pledges that its electors will not vote for its own statewide winner, but for the winner of the _national_ popular vote across all 50 states and D.C. The compact has a built-in trigger: it does nothing until member states collectively hold **270** electoral votes -- the number needed to win. At that moment, without one word of the Constitution changing, the presidency becomes a national popular-vote prize. Whoever wins the most votes in America wins the electors of every compact state.
**The scoreboard**
As of this month, 18 states plus the District of Columbia have enacted it -- California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, Virginia, Vermont and Washington -- totaling **222 electoral votes, 82 percent of the way there. Forty-eight to go.**
Watch how they got here: Maine came aboard in 2024. Virginia -- a 13-vote state with a newly elected Democratic trifecta -- signed in April 2026. And the November midterms just delivered the movement its best map yet. As Politico reported a week after the election, the remaining path is explicit: **Pennsylvania (19), Michigan (15) and Wisconsin (10), plus either Arizona (11) or Nevada (6)** , and the compact activates -- plausibly in time to govern the 2028 election. For the first time, the people who want the Electoral College gone hold, or plausibly hold, the votes to finish it.
**The map nobody mentions**
Here's the part of the story that gets no airtime. Per the National Conference of State Legislatures, **14 states require no ID document of any kind to vote in person** -- you state your name, you sign the poll book, you get a ballot: California, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, Pennsylvania and Vermont. Add D.C., and that is **198 electoral votes -- more than a third of the entire Electoral College -- cast under no-document rules.**
The five largest states on that list are California, New York, Pennsylvania, Illinois and New Jersey -- 134 electoral votes between them.
Now cross-reference with the compact. Twelve of the 19 member jurisdictions -- **170 of its 222 electoral votes** -- are no-ID states. And of the 48 votes still needed to trigger it, Pennsylvania's 19 and Nevada's 6 -- 25 of the 48 -- sit in no-ID states. Pennsylvania is the crown jewel: the biggest prize on the board, the classic kingmaker, and a state where nobody is asked for identification.
**The argument**
Defenders will say: relax. Voters still sign the poll book, signatures can be audited, and prosecuted cases of illegal voting are vanishingly rare. All true. But I don't need to believe in ballot-stuffing conspiracies to see the problem, and neither should you.
The problem is asymmetry and stakes. In 2024, roughly 1.5 points separated the candidates nationally. Had the compact been active, the presidency would have turned on the aggregate national total -- every marginal vote in every state counted equally. When every vote counts equally, the integrity of every jurisdiction's checking process counts equally too. A system in which one coalition's votes run 198 electors deep in states that ask no questions, while the other's strongholds check photo ID at the door, is not one system. It is two different rulebooks wired together, and the presidency gets decided on the difference.
Elections do not need _documented_ fraud to lose legitimacy; they need the _appearance of opportunity_. Ask any losing side after any close count, in any country, what they concluded. A compact triggered on this map would put the White House within reach of whichever coalition can best maximize turnout in the jurisdictions where a signature is the only check. That is not a conspiracy theory. It is a plain description of the rules on offer for 2028.
If a national popular vote is what we want, fine -- argue for it in the open, honestly. But a national count is only as trustworthy as its weakest checkpoint. The obvious complement to a national vote count is uniform voter ID -- free, easy access, applied everywhere. The compact does the opposite: it aggregates the country's ballots without harmonizing the country's safeguards.
**What to watch**
The next move is not in Washington. It is in statehouses. Pennsylvania, Michigan and Wisconsin in the 2027 legislative sessions; Nevada as the cheap closer at six votes. Forty-eight electoral votes, four or five states, one trigger. After that, the Constitution is untouched and the Electoral College is functionally gone -- and the rules under which the next president is chosen will have been set, disproportionately, by the states that ask the fewest questions at the door.
Cobble is the right word. Watch the cobblers work.

Repeal would take a constitutional amendment -- two-thirds of Congress, then 38 states. Dead on arrival, and both sides know it. Republicans got crushed in the midterms — now they’re trying to run our playbook.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261114-1&t=1&akid=4248%2E587540%2EWbMoLw)
**A Leaders We Deserve dupe just dropped, Peter — and it’s got a right-wing megadonor behind it.**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261114_1_mm.IGpf8Y&refcode=em20261114-4248&amount=5&t=2&akid=4248%2E587540%2EWbMoLw)

Let me explain.
Last Tuesday, Republicans took a beating up and down the ballot. Our endorsed candidates flipped 13 seats from red to blue, won 8 federal seats helping flip the House and Senate, and sent a loud and clear message across the country that young, bold progressives are the way to win.
Less than a week later, a new Republican group launched with a mission to recruit young candidates, train them, and elect the next generation of far-right candidates in 2028.
Their message? Their party has gotten too out of touch, too old, and too weak to win.
_Huh._ Wonder where they got that idea.
Besides launching a GOP knockoff of what our movement has been building from the start, here’s the part that should really worry you: **they launched with $12 million from a single right-wing megadonor who also chairs the board of one of the think tanks behind MAGA’s agenda.**
That’s what we’re up against. A megadonor-backed operation built to copy our strategy and drown out the next generation progressives we just got across the finish line.
We aren’t going to sit around and let that happen.
Our power has always come from grassroots supporters like you, chipping in what you can, when you can. Right now, we need a little bit more of that power to keep building our pipeline of young leaders for 2028.
**[Will you pitch in $5 to help us hit our $60,000 midmonth goal and stay ahead of the game for the next cycle?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261114_1_mm.IGpf8Y&refcode=em20261114-4248&amount=5&t=4&akid=4248%2E587540%2EWbMoLw)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

name: Rep. Gloria Johnson
subject: Two fighters emerge: Don Leonard and Angela Gonzales-Torres are standing up!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY FRIENDS OF GLORIA JOHNSON, LISA SORENSEN, TREASURER
body:
I want to share actions you can take from my friend Corbin Trent, because who leads our fight matters.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/c269bc74d178/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7364026?e=dc5f639d62)
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
|
---
| | Hey Friends!
Democrats have made historic gains, but there is much work to do. Leadership matters and we need bold leadership that will put the people first. I know that many of you understand this and want something new. That is why I am sharing my friend Corbin Trent’s email—it gives you steps to make your voice heard in this upcoming decision. I am just going to post his email below....
In solidarity,Gloria

“Good morning, folks. And a good morning it is. My apologies for any typos. This is a completely dictated, unedited email. I am trying to launch an ad campaign, a massive polling series, and parent 4 kids...But! Pressure is building against leadership. In the United States Senate, we’re seeing more and more senators go on the record saying no to Chuck Schumer. It ain’t over but the efforts are working.Now, the tough nut to crack, of course, is the House of Representatives and Hakeem Jeffries. The people are speaking up. The polling is clear but representatives have a hard time listening once they’re in the swamp. Amazingly, two people: Don Leonard and Angela Gonzalez-Torres have taken the courageous step of saying no to Hakeem. As many of you know, I was the communications director for Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez during her first campaign and then her first term on the Hill. One of the things that made her able to be the independent-minded representative that she was is financial support from a massive number of people. She could not be threatened with having her campaign support removed. She could not be threatened with not getting a committee assignment that gets her enough airtime that she can raise more money. She had a base of people willing to financially support her. We need to recreate that for these people that are taking a stand. I need you to donate to these people. Here, you can split your money between them. And there are some people that are going to give a lot of money, and some people that are going to give a little. It really doesn’t matter how much you put in. In D.C., money talks, period. And your money can speak volumes.[**$5, $10, Doesn’t matter, man. Click this link, put in some cash, please. It’s the most important thing that you can do to have different leadership in DC.**](https://us.list-manage.com/ySboChDqrNt?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) excitingly, we are going to be able to run the polling that I told you about yesterday. We’re also going to be able to run ads in D.C., making sure that these representatives know what’s happening outside of the bubble that they find themselves in during freshman orientation.This leadership fight in the House and in the Senate is one of the first opportunities we have to make sure that the people’s voices are not only heard but heeded. So we’re all going to have to come together and do some of the work. What can you do? Well, let me tell you what you can do. Here’s a list:[**Sign the petition started to draft Ayanna Pressley**](https://us.list-manage.com/196td_jLtpx?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) for Speaker. It doesn’t matter if you prefer her or not. What we need is somebody brave enough to step up and run. Then the emperor will be shown to be wearing no clothes. Click the image to use the tool to contact your Democratic Reps or call the switchboard at **(202) 224-3121**[****](https://us.list-manage.com/Q6EAQbTqSf6?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)

Right now, the voters are being loud. We’re speaking up. We’re signing petitions, calling Representatives and Senators, and applying pressure. If we keep this up, what we can show is that democracy still matters in the Democratic Party, that voters still matter, that our opinions matter. Win, lose, or draw, these fights are important because they’re allowing us to build the muscle memory and the systems to have these battles. This is going to be the first of many. So if you want change, if you want Medicare for all, if you want a health care system that provides services for people at a reasonable price and rapid speed, if you want an economy where people can afford housing and health care, childcare, where we’re not subject to the whims of a few, but the needs of the many are what drives our policy, then we’re going to go through fights just like this over and over until the people have more power. But again, the most important thing we can do is empower the people that stand up and give them a safety net that allows them to take a stand for us the against the powerful people in the party. [So please click this link and donate to Angela Gonzales - Torres and Don Leonard. ](https://us.list-manage.com/yCtpO1atT1H?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)Thank you for being here,Corbin Trent

Madison Brooks, a 19-year-old LSU sophomore, died on January 15, 2023, after being struck by a car on Airline Highway in the pre-dawn hours. Prosecutors say she was raped earlier that night by more than one of four men who had left a Baton Rouge bar with her; the men say any sexual contact was consensual. Four were arrested; three remain charged -- Desmond Carter, Casen Carver, and Kaivon Washington. None has been tried; all are presumed innocent.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fed0ce12-cf6d-4d88-9357-70c1637b2e65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The judge and her son**
The cases landed with Judge Gail Horne Ray of the 19th Judicial District Court -- and that's where the story gets its twist. Court records and local reporting (The Advocate, WBRZ, WAFB) establish that her son, Nelson Dan Taylor Jr., pleaded guilty in the late 1990s to multiple rapes -- counts of forcible and aggravated rape, plus aggravated burglaries -- with victims who were teenage girls, reportedly including classmates from his Baton Rouge high school. Ray, then a practicing lawyer, was his defense attorney.
Taylor, now 46, went back to court this year seeking to have those convictions set aside. Last year he pleaded guilty to an obscenity charge from a 2024 hotel incident -- allegedly exposing himself to a hotel worker -- while he was already on probation. Because judges customarily recuse themselves from matters involving a colleague's family, his filings end up in front of the one judge in the building who can't recuse: his mother.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/620c8790-fcec-41d3-8138-fabacd5ffc3b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The recusal war**
Once the son's history surfaced, District Attorney Hillar Moore moved to remove Ray from Carver's trial. The motion leaned on text messages Carver sent his father -- including "her son was accused of rape a while back so she knows to help us," and claims they were "friends with the judge." On November 3, 2025, Judge Brad Myers granted the recusal, and the First Circuit affirmed.
Then the Louisiana Supreme Court reversed it. In May 2026 it ruled that prosecutors had failed to prove why Ray should be removed, and it later denied a rehearing bid -- reinstating her. When the story went national in August (Fox News, New York Post), the DA pressed again to remove her from the cases against all three defendants; the state's highest court has left her in place. So the post's core claim -- lower courts ordered her off, the Supreme Court kept her on -- is accurate, just condensed.
Critics also point to a pattern: local outlets report the DA separately asked the Supreme Court to void Ray's ruling that threw out another man's rape conviction -- after that defendant had asked her to reduce his sentence so he could seek parole.
**The pink-clothing sideshow**
Over the summer, a defense attorney filed a motion asking to bar spectators from wearing pink -- Brooks' family and friends wear it in her memory -- arguing it was courtroom advocacy. Ray ruled in August that pink was allowed, though not shirts bearing Brooks' image. This month she found attorney Caitlin Fowlkes in contempt for using Brooks' full name in that motion, then declined to impose any penalty beyond an admonition.
**What it actually tests**
Louisiana law requires a judge to step aside when partiality is proven or when her impartiality "might reasonably be questioned" -- but the burden sits on whoever moves for recusal, and the Supreme Court found the state hadn't met it. The irony is symmetrical: the defendant's own texts said the judge "knows to help us," while prosecutors argued that a judge who once defended her son against serial rape charges shouldn't now be deciding rape charges. Neither proves actual bias; both are reasons a reasonable observer might doubt neutrality. That gap -- between what can be legally proven and what the public can unsee -- is the entire story.
One caveat: the post's race-first framing (Black judge, white victim) is not what any filing argues. The legal fight has been entirely about family history, appearance of fairness, and who bears the burden of proving doubt.
**Where it stands**
Carver faces a bench trial in late November; Carter a jury trial on December 7 -- both before Ray, with Washington's case still pending. For the Brooks family, every ruling in the coming weeks will come from the one judge in the courthouse whose own family file contains the crime their daughter's case is about. Louisiana's highest court has decided that's legally survivable. Whether it looks like justice -- to them, or to anyone watching -- is the question her courtroom will answer by Christmas.

body:
Sharing stories from Ground Truth and what we’ve learned.
#
Hi there,
By now, you’ve probably seen plenty of statistics about the midterm elections. Who turned out, which groups shifted their support, and what issues drove voters to the polls. But behind all of those numbers are individual people with their own reasons for voting, not voting, changing their minds, or deciding to get involved.
We want to share a few of their stories with you.
This year, Swing Left volunteers had real, meaningful, and impactful conversations with voters through [**Ground Truth**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3281?t=1&akid=3436%2E1562180%2ERz1f6H), our innovative, listening-first voter contact program. Rather than launching into a pitch about a candidate, volunteers were trained to take a listening-first approach and ask people how they felt about the direction of the country—and why. They took the time to hear people out, and many conversations lasted upwards of 10 minutes.
In some conversations, volunteers helped voters see a reason to support a Democratic candidate or participate in the election when they hadn’t planned to before. These are the kinds of voters we see as persuadable, and their stories offer a window into what can happen when volunteers take the time to listen, answer questions, and help connect the stakes of an election to people’s everyday lives.
Below are a few examples from Ground Truth conversations in swing districts and states this year:
> **A young, small business owner unsure whether his vote mattered commits to vote for Democrats**
> In San Benito, Texas, a volunteer called Jose, a young small business owner who drives a truck. Fuel prices had hit him hard, and he was upset about ICE agents harassing people in his community. He wants them screened, trained, wearing body cameras, and held accountable. At first, he wasn’t sure he’d vote at all, because he didn’t think anything would change. But when he heard how narrowly his representative won the last election, he realized his vote could make a difference.**By the end of the call, he committed to voting for Democrats in November, and he even said he was interested in volunteering to reach Spanish-speaking voters.**
> **Discouraged 74-year-old Democrat goes from “0” to “voting”***
> In Sierra Vista, Arizona, a volunteer spoke with Margaret, a lifelong Democrat in her 70s. She told our volunteer she was a 0 on voting this year. She’s struggling to get by, and she felt like no elected official had ever helped her. To her, it seemed like government was just getting richer while she struggled every day. **But when our volunteer explained what a Democratic House majority could do and how close we were to winning one, she was persuaded to vote.**
> **Woman juggling necessary expenses moves from “5” to “10”***
> In Pennsylvania, a volunteer knocked on Claudia’s door. She was struggling to afford groceries, heating oil, and gas for her family, and she’d missed the last election because of work. She started at a 5 on voting Democratic because she hadn’t looked at the candidates yet. After hearing about the Democratic candidate’s record and the cuts to health care and school food programs the Republican candidate had voted for, she said she would definitely vote for the Democrat: “A 10.” **She made a plan to vote early and even filled out postcards to follow up with three people in her life to encourage them to vote as well.**
> **Young voter goes from “0” to “10” once she sees healthcare cuts would hit her***
> In Milwaukie, Oregon, volunteers met Jacqueline, a 20-year-old voter who said she was a zero on voting because she didn’t have enough information. As they walked through the differences between the two House candidates, she realized the proposed cuts to healthcare would affect her personally, since she relies on the Oregon Health Plan. As the Ground Truth volunteers started to leave, she said she was absolutely going to vote.
These volunteer-recounted stories show what’s possible when we take the time to listen to voters instead of jumping in to persuade them right away. Many voters weren’t hostile to Democrats—they just felt like no one was paying attention to them, and they didn’t have the information they needed to see what was at stake.
Thanks to Ground Truth, we’re not losing what we learn from these voters. These stories are made available to campaigns and party committees and saved so they can be used in the next election, too. It’s a new way of organizing, and one that has real potential for the years ahead.
These stories are just a glimpse of what our volunteers heard on the ground this year. [**If you want to hear more about what we learned and what it means for the elections ahead, join us on Thursday, November 19th, for our virtual post-election Inside Update call.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3282?t=2&akid=3436%2E1562180%2ERz1f6H)
**[RSVP Now »](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3282?t=3&akid=3436%2E1562180%2ERz1f6H)**
This is the work Swing Left will carry into 2027 and 2028. We’ll be back soon to share more stories from the field this year!
— The Swing Left Team

_*Volunteers asked the people they spoke with to rank themselves between 0-10 on their likelihood to vote, as well as their likelihood to vote for the Democratic candidate._

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261114-1&t=4&refcode2=3436_1562180_Rz1f6H&akid=3436%2E1562180%2ERz1f6H)

At first, he wasn’t sure he’d vote at all, because he didn’t think anything would change. But when he heard how narrowly his representative won the last election, he realized his vote could make a difference.By the end of the call, he committed to voting for Democrats in November, and he even said he was interested in volunteering to reach Spanish-speaking voters. Discouraged 74-year-old Democrat goes from “0” to “voting” In Sierra Vista, Arizona, a volunteer spoke with Margaret, a lifelong Democrat in her 70s. She told our volunteer she was a 0 on voting this year. She’s struggling to get by, and she felt like no elected official had ever helped her. To her, it seemed like government was just getting richer while she struggled every day. But when our volunteer explained what a Democratic House majority could do and how close we were to winning one, she was persuaded to vote. Woman juggling necessary expenses moves from “5” to “10”* In Pennsylvania, a volunteer knocked on Claudia’s door. She was struggling to afford groceries, heating oil, and gas for her family, and she’d missed the last election because of work. She started at a 5 on voting Democratic because she hadn’t looked at the candidates yet. After hearing about the Democratic candidate’s record and the cuts to health care and school food programs the Republican candidate had voted for, she said she would definitely vote for the Democrat: “A 10.” She made a plan to vote early and even filled out postcards to follow up with three people in her life to encourage them to vote as well. Young voter goes from “0” to “10” once she sees healthcare cuts would hit her* In Milwaukie, Oregon, volunteers met Jacqueline, a 20-year-old voter who said she was a zero on voting because she didn’t have enough information. As they walked through the differences between the two House candidates, she realized the proposed cuts to healthcare would affect her personally, since she relies on the Oregon Health Plan. As the Ground Truth volunteers started to leave, she said she was absolutely going to vote. These volunteer-recounted stories show what’s possible when we take the time to listen to voters instead of jumping in to persuade them right away. Many voters weren’t hostile to Democrats—they just felt like no one was paying attention to them, and they didn’t have the information they needed to see what was at stake. Thanks to Ground Truth, we’re not losing what we learn from these voters. These stories are made available to campaigns and party committees and saved so they can be used in the next election, too. It’s a new way of organizing, and one that has real potential for the years ahead. These stories are just a glimpse of what our volunteers heard on the ground this year. This is the work Swing Left will carry into 2027 and 2028. We’ll be back soon to share more stories from the field this year! — The Swing Left Team Volunteers asked the people they spoke with to rank themselves between 0-10 on their likelihood to vote, as well as their likelihood to vote for the Democratic candidate. Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power. | | | ---|---|---|--- Paid for by Swing Left, , not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. Marco Polo, the nonprofit research group that spent years on the Biden laptop, announced its next project Tuesday: the federal judiciary.
Founder Garrett Ziegler says the group decided "a new multi-year beat is needed." He calls federal judges "a new caste system in the United States."
[| | | | | Marco Polo
---
@MarcoPolo501c3
Watch & hear abt what we're doing next. Federal judges are an elite caste in America, and the public is in the dark abt many of their machinations. In other words, they're a worthy topic of our inquiry. This new beat should be fun and, more importantly, extremely revelatory.
| 5:51 PM * Nov 10, 20261.59K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/2329cc68-997f-494e-8d6b-0fe6de736246?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The project is a website, [ThirdBranch.icu](https://substack.com/redirect/29240dbe-7f6e-4f92-887c-d781412cedc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Its own description: a directory of the Senate-confirmed federal judiciary that "details every judge's professional & family connections & any potential conflicts that could/should warrant recusal."
In the video, Ziegler promises financial disclosures, "who they're married to, what their adult children are doing." He says there will be more than 1,400 profiles "in the next year plus," and that "there's going to be no subscription sold." He also asks for tips from anyone with experience before these judges. He says the profiles aren't all built yet.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..Z9n7LQvAB-YgzgZ3N1TsUAsWhvcohCENEwbFs4ccaOE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=224391431)
His case against the bench: lifetime jobs, big pay, and "senior status" that he says keeps the pay.
The federal courts' [salary table](https://substack.com/redirect/77bda9f4-3a56-4b25-9d5d-b6f4b2dc96cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has district judges at $249,900 and circuit judges at $264,900 for 2026 (salary). He also says only eight judges since 1789 have been impeached and removed, making a federal judgeship one of the most lucrative tenured jobs in America. The [Federal Judicial Center's list](https://substack.com/redirect/44b3f3f1-930c-4397-a540-4e20180fc98e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has eight.
Maine's federal bench is small, and the public record on it is already thick. However, the judicial transparency website is fairly thin on new disclosures.
**The district court:** Chief Judge [Lance Walker](https://substack.com/redirect/af1983f1-e062-4958-b05a-5919ed5cfaa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was nominated by Donald Trump and confirmed in October 2018. He became chief in 2024. [Stacey Neumann](https://substack.com/redirect/d9648628-1bd8-49b4-8144-182db328024e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was nominated by Joe Biden and confirmed in July 2024. Before that she was an assistant U.S. attorney and sat on Maine's ethics and election commission. Judge John Woodcock has been on the court since 2003. Nancy Torresen took senior status on October 11, 2025. As of November 10, her seat is [still vacant](https://substack.com/redirect/dbf384e7-c9e3-4c82-b82c-6f0ebf4330bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with no nominee listed.
**The appeals court:** Joshua Dunlap, a Portland private-practice lawyer until then, was [nominated by Trump and confirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/b2e992b8-7d99-4035-9efb-4a81c92fca71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the First Circuit on November 4, 2025, by a [52-46 vote](https://substack.com/redirect/6f711432-45a4-4197-bc25-4a08cac373f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
**What they've ruled.**
Voter data: On May 21, 2026, Walker [dismissed the Justice Department's suit](https://substack.com/redirect/50dc05ba-05e1-41f5-af32-47f6b8adbaa2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) demanding Maine's unredacted voter list, writing that "states are the primary regulators and administrators of elections for federal office, unless Congress passes legislation that preempts that framework." In other words, a Trump appointee blocked the Trump Administration's effort to purge non-citizens from Maine's voter rolls.
School funding: On April 11, 2025, Woodcock [ordered USDA to release](https://substack.com/redirect/e48004b1-b6ea-47b7-b29d-d3e4ea5c1b31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) funds it froze over Maine's transgender athlete policy. The order said it wasn't weighing in on that dispute, only on whether USDA followed required procedure.
ICE: In [January 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/03546edf-4374-4d54-8c8d-2bc8ce48cf7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Woodcock ordered two men returned to Maine after ICE moved them against a court order. In [June](https://substack.com/redirect/b5474a13-9e1b-4b92-a282-33dfa579714f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Neumann ordered a Lewiston man released after the same thing.
Sentencing: The Maine Wire reported Neumann gave [Ken Yiu time served](https://substack.com/redirect/6aaf6650-b195-4bf7-acc8-580d8758bf2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on a mortgage fraud and grow-house case. Neumann, like Maine's state judges, has been bizarrely lenient with the few members of Chinese cannabis cartels who end up in court.

name: Bill Gray
subject: Restoring hope in our country
body:
Before Michelangelo painted “The Creation of Adam,” before Rembrandt painted “The Sacrifice of Isaac,” there were the words that inspired them...

| | | This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuq2zAQhp9G3tno4sjOwosQx4ezSA-noXRpFGnsDOiGJKfk7YshfYFu5xvmZ77_93W-KrTo1x_KwYA5zyaYOUEuIaFfHyEC-rAlHTZf0mvmlMuasZq1s9IFnzC3qjLDgbN-6SsYWHdspWQtZdVjOC53I-X9wED3Lb1rOCxCLmphouvMUXYVDvs9xljLBBWcNhwUPXBoKev5AuxIWrpFowo06DMayDqEGIPFgjo3Ia2VHR6lxEzEifCJ8CmD3hI0D7Q2G2WhAbMRPpngVYGdbzGGVOo1gSq1cpBQK1_v_75q8zRETBlWB76cgwEiRipYL0-UTufr5WP8Gi-Xb8LlVtycdy_7SkwhR9AF_fpGDgxujogRnEL7HmrlosLVEzFa5U1YdrvznvnmwRfwhYhx_Lydv379PH1cxvm7qz9vt_qfqCoNJv5BazHLjrR03QMaHVxV_re-58D_BgAA__8yjq11) Fellow Patriot, [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuq2zAQhp9G3tno4sjOwosQx4ezSA-noXRpFGnsDOiGJKfk7YshfYFu5xvmZ77_93W-KrTo1x_KwYA5zyaYOUEuIaFfHyEC-rAlHTZf0mvmlMuasZq1s9IFnzC3qjLDgbN-6SsYWHdspWQtZdVjOC53I-X9wED3Lb1rOCxCLmphouvMUXYVDvs9xljLBBWcNhwUPXBoKev5AuxIWrpFowo06DMayDqEGIPFgjo3Ia2VHR6lxEzEifCJ8CmD3hI0D7Q2G2WhAbMRPpngVYGdbzGGVOo1gSq1cpBQK1_v_75q8zRETBlWB76cgwEiRipYL0-UTufr5WP8Gi-Xb8LlVtycdy_7SkwhR9AF_fpGDgxujogRnEL7HmrlosLVEzFa5U1YdrvznvnmwRfwhYhx_Lydv379PH1cxvm7qz9vt_qfqCoNJv5BazHLjrR03QMaHVxV_re-58D_BgAA__8yjq11) You may be discouraged by the Left’s dominance over our colleges and universities, and its growing influence over K-12 education. But we must not lose **hope**. Instead, we must fight back with the **TRUTH**! Hillsdale College has been engaging the Left on the battlefield of education for decades. That’s why we’ve turned our course, [**“The Great American Story: A Land of Hope”**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuq2zAQhp9G3tno4sjOwosQx4ezSA-noXRpFGnsDOiGJKfk7YshfYFu5xvmZ77_93W-KrTo1x_KwYA5zyaYOUEuIaFfHyEC-rAlHTZf0mvmlMuasZq1s9IFnzC3qjLDgbN-6SsYWHdspWQtZdVjOC53I-X9wED3Lb1rOCxCLmphouvMUXYVDvs9xljLBBWcNhwUPXBoKev5AuxIWrpFowo06DMayDqEGIPFgjo3Ia2VHR6lxEzEifCJ8CmD3hI0D7Q2G2WhAbMRPpngVYGdbzGGVOo1gSq1cpBQK1_v_75q8zRETBlWB76cgwEiRipYL0-UTufr5WP8Gi-Xb8LlVtycdy_7SkwhR9AF_fpGDgxujogRnEL7HmrlosLVEzFa5U1YdrvznvnmwRfwhYhx_Lydv379PH1cxvm7qz9vt_qfqCoNJv5BazHLjrR03QMaHVxV_re-58D_BgAA__8yjq11) into a DVD set, and I’d like you to have a copy. Taught by historian Wilfred McClay and based on his published history of America, **“The Great American Story: A Land of Hope”** presents a full, unbiased account of America’s past. Hillsdale’s goal in producing this course is to **restore the kind of intelligent patriotism—especially among our young people—that is _essential_ to preserving free government.** **“The Great American Story: A Land of Hope”** is a powerful counterweight to _The New York Times’_ “1619 Project,” which is injecting the idea that America is an essentially unjust nation into our K-12 schools. Please consider getting [**“The Great American Story: A Land of Hope”**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuq2zAQhp9G3tno4sjOwosQx4ezSA-noXRpFGnsDOiGJKfk7YshfYFu5xvmZ77_93W-KrTo1x_KwYA5zyaYOUEuIaFfHyEC-rAlHTZf0mvmlMuasZq1s9IFnzC3qjLDgbN-6SsYWHdspWQtZdVjOC53I-X9wED3Lb1rOCxCLmphouvMUXYVDvs9xljLBBWcNhwUPXBoKev5AuxIWrpFowo06DMayDqEGIPFgjo3Ia2VHR6lxEzEifCJ8CmD3hI0D7Q2G2WhAbMRPpngVYGdbzGGVOo1gSq1cpBQK1_v_75q8zRETBlWB76cgwEiRipYL0-UTufr5WP8Gi-Xb8LlVtycdy_7SkwhR9AF_fpGDgxujogRnEL7HmrlosLVEzFa5U1YdrvznvnmwRfwhYhx_Lydv379PH1cxvm7qz9vt_qfqCoNJv5BazHLjrR03QMaHVxV_re-58D_BgAA__8yjq11) as a DVD set for your home library or to give as a gift. Presenting true American history is the surest means of preserving liberty. Quantities are limited, so reserve your copy today. [**https://secure.hillsdale.edu/donate/support-great-american-story-dvd**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuq2zAQhp9G3tno4sjOwosQx4ezSA-noXRpFGnsDOiGJKfk7YshfYFu5xvmZ77_93W-KrTo1x_KwYA5zyaYOUEuIaFfHyEC-rAlHTZf0mvmlMuasZq1s9IFnzC3qjLDgbN-6SsYWHdspWQtZdVjOC53I-X9wED3Lb1rOCxCLmphouvMUXYVDvs9xljLBBWcNhwUPXBoKev5AuxIWrpFowo06DMayDqEGIPFgjo3Ia2VHR6lxEzEifCJ8CmD3hI0D7Q2G2WhAbMRPpngVYGdbzGGVOo1gSq1cpBQK1_v_75q8zRETBlWB76cgwEiRipYL0-UTufr5WP8Gi-Xb8LlVtycdy_7SkwhR9AF_fpGDgxujogRnEL7HmrlosLVEzFa5U1YdrvznvnmwRfwhYhx_Lydv379PH1cxvm7qz9vt_qfqCoNJv5BazHLjrR03QMaHVxV_re-58D_BgAA__8yjq11) Thank you for your partnership with Hillsdale College and your support of its mission on behalf of liberty. **Good Morning!** On this day in 1896, future first lady [Mamie Doud Eisenhower](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFv8yAQgOFfY2-xfIAhDAzfki3f2hERc9ioxIcOFCv_vmq3zl3f4Rnej7u_h1zysf0PT3R9Tf7AsxXsHdl_HnQWbCkzMlbiXqnktnHwYhb6AnAB5StTq7h2D2N0KYk16BEdGKu0BrUs4-4AY7RWx4dBKczyWKyRymKIVxUNquuY3TcIAArkrGCZgkxXM8-LsKi1VHJQM8bciae-40qFOERK5U0v5Gml51jc3nttg_w3iNsgbpgbHjudyCU_OPB72uj1q7eRXaxnLiU3bQY1b8-Qyw_W_zri5cRXAAAA__85V3Ua) was born in Boone, Iowa. She grew up in Denver and married Dwight Eisenhower in her family's Lafayette Street home in 1916. The _Colorado Flyover_ has passed 300,000 subscribers, enough readers to fill Empower Field at Mile High nearly four times! We're celebrating that Coloradans are opting for factual news that lets you draw your own conclusions. Thank you for trusting us with the first few minutes of your day. If the _Colorado Flyover_ has earned a spot in your routine, forward this email to a friend and help us find the next 300,000. After this week's Veterans Day, our inbox filled up with stories about the people in your lives who served our country. So we asked ourselves: How do we serve the people who served us? It turns out there are seven benefits many military families never claim, and most of them are free, from property tax breaks to burial honors you can request years after the funeral. ## Report Details Knowles Fire Deaths

## FAA Issues Nationwide Ground Stop
The Federal Aviation Administration [ordered a nationwide ground stop](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OrDAMBeCnCV1G-SMZihS3oZvbboksYsBShiDwMNp5-lXYR9jaln2-8_UYHkCZ1vk_PDEyfKZhxfeRkRn3YQJYgamsb0o47-W1poPLtpTBKOOl1lK7AUamEwcHTYrWj11wDUYdOue9bm1olmhABURnk7OoAoDybTJmSl3y-t55aCjWe1prp61qrbul1qK-Bz_6gL41RjiFibjsN14QdvqUFab8XU7cb2N5NjkuzNsh7D9hemF62KqijoTpM50oTP-bX1aAhJMul5wyzQsfsq7L15aA8bhcVtZIzR7T9qac6fBBODU_gfL1kf9a1hnNTwAAAP__voB_GA) Friday, halting departures at all U.S. airports after communications problems affected multiple air route traffic control centers. Flights already in the air were allowed to continue to their destinations. The [FAA said every flight was accounted for](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DuO5CAYBODT4AyLl2EdEGzirDfd0PrNo_1LNLQAtzV9-pFngjnAxCVV6av_t_UGmDDf_8Ej2A7vuOZwthR6D3WNABk6lnyiD_dajuxbL8-9rIIJTTmnXK3gOr7CqmDwVmo3GzUEy82stOaTNMNutWF-25jnwhitIouRKcZnKZ1Q8yb0gPbq45wrLtkk1egnGfgfo502QU9CEMWCx17q2PcAFd8lQ0wf5RXq6MpjSHbv_dmI_EvEQsRynucIm-PTlRKxHI1eLCKWCECxtSM0-kOj3zZ64WjJ9GgUsNJeIUZ0Q7X-eWJK2LQhit0fgOlrtv_2sZcVnwEAAP__9VyBew), with international arrivals handled case by case. The stop began shortly before 4 p.m. EST and was lifted shortly after 8 p.m. The FAA [told Fox News](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LuOqzAQBuCngc7IN-xQuDgNXU67JZo14zCSsSPswG6efkVS7ANsOZqL5vs_rtMVKFK6_YcVXYVnmBIeJWKtuE0BIEGlnA6a8bblR5pLzfclT5JLw4RgQk_gK-04aWhnp4wfrG7RCTtoY0SvbLu4YPkQes4NQu_hU_AguboI00tl1MUPLbnznhBCC8V7pbu5Vygu1nhj0fRSNprjTDVvXV0QNnrmBCF-5x23zue1jW6p9V4a9a-RYyPH4zi6kL9Oytlv5BhpR3bWjRwDAKNSHljYL4-9fewEMk8VC_N5XR-J_GumvFfazc33g2KkYmyj-W0Fiq8f6l_j2538CQAA__-bC4fi) the outage was not a cyberattack, and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said it posed no threat to public safety. In Arizona, departures were [grounded at Phoenix Sky Harbor, Mesa Gateway, Scottsdale, and other airports](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAQhU9jMiP8TwcONiHrTTdEhV1uLBmMbG-j7tOPmBlpDjBJRaXvvff9u893iCnuj7-woW3wDvOOZ03YGpY5AOzQYt7P6PFR8v_d15aPNc984JoyRpmcwbX4xFlC563Q7mZkh5aZm9SaKWG61epbwBAEAzWoUQzGCTW6xY2D8wKXsHTRXjzGmGRiUEL2Xglko9FOG9SKcyIH9LHl0rcVocR33iGkV35i6V3eumTX1o5KxB_CJ8Kn8zx7eAfYYnpdD4RPVwLhE2PXEYRPEMuRS6sUXMm10m8shRDQNfR0edGf9TQA0C8F9HJA-NQV648zphSrNkQOjw1i-qzTfmvyaflHAAAA__-6m4mS). This is just the second time since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks that the FAA has issued a nationwide ground stop. The only other case since was January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned.
## Mayes Seeks Execution for Trooper's Killer
Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes asked the state Supreme Court to [set a Jan. 27 execution date](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2unDAUhVdjOiOuf0PhIg3dS5sS3dgXcJ6xkfEMmVl9RJQdvOZUR9_5-fkxf2BMMa8_cCfX8L3Mma4zUWtU5wUxY4slXzHQWssjh7OVYyuzGIThABzUjL7FJ80Ku-Ck8aNVHTmwozIGtLTd5oxexC8L3grtQY1BG5TSkxLjaBcaoIvu5gGAAjloqfqgJcE3a7yxZLQQTA0UYiu1bxthje-ScUmv8qTa-7J3yW2tHSeT35mYmJiu6-rxveAe0-s2MDHdCUxMALdIJqb_GI4rx_Pz5L8xc2E5_SH_uDfzgI34jplfW-GfMSUKvNVSDqocxlEzMXXVheOKKcXTWKaGdceY_jVqXz3z6cTfAAAA__9nE4fj) for the man who killed a state trooper on the Beeline Highway in 1995. Ernesto Martinez shot and killed Trooper Bob Martin, 57, [a 27-year DPS veteran](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OhCAYxJ8GO4z8EbSguMZur73SfMKnkrBgkJXsPv1lN_cG181kkpnJ7-c238AHH7dvuKMp8FrniPUMWArmeQWIUHyK1TvccnpEd5Z07GnmHVeUMcrkDLb4C2cJjTNC2VHLBg3To1SK9UI3uwFrHcNFs5EPWiirFivGQTDbiUWoZW28efcxxiQTXS9k63qBbNDKKo2q55zIDp0vKbdlR8j-lSKs4ZkuzK1N9yaYvZTjJOKL8InwqdbaOjwxY3nnhE9sHHvCp-Et1cezQY-CEz5dWDBDpGldvcVMt0eM6KhLNdIU6d8c3f22V3jSHekBJacQ0BE-Ndm4o_oQ_Kk0kd12Bx8-p8p_eV6G_wYAAP__ayWJmg), during a traffic stop north of Shea Boulevard on Aug. 15, 1995. During two days on the run, Martinez killed a second person in California before he was captured. He was convicted in 1997 and sentenced to death the next year, and prosecutors say he has [exhausted his state and federal appeals](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp8GOiP8gwmFi23osu2WaGIPwRLY7DDE2Tz9iqv7Brf_dPSd8-c-3SGuMT1_w4aO4TNPCcuxIjPSNAMk4JhTiQGflM8UDs77kifVKiukFNJM4Dm-cDJQB6etH3pTo5P9YKyVne7rxWFneuOHR7Cgzc0af1MPb7RXqmuD0lBHd_GklEbqttOmCZ1Geeuttz3aTqnKtBgiZ2p4QaD4yQnm9V9-ITU-b_XqFub9qPSvSo2VGkspzZzfst2XjCm-r1GlxkutUuM3QBD-PfHgQ-Ab_Xl5igJEkFggJTw4iw2IY8KPkMPQCaacdySxnRSQanJhL3Fd42H7yrTPDeL6dYd_WvLl1P8AAAD__8X8i9s). They argue that a 2019 court challenge he filed, which is still pending, doesn’t stand in the way. Martinez’s lawyer has [accused Mayes of rushing the execution](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFywjAMgOGncTY4W5aVZPDQJRtdO-ZErBDfmZhLBLQ8fY--Qtd_-Ib_6zSeOJe8Xj75KlH5NY-rPPciqrKNM_PKmuv6zEkuW72vadd6W-oIFujg3MHhyJPmh4zITYqepr7FRqJreyRywbfNEs_dOc0EPkCHYD0gJnuWuUPyFIKjJse355xD523weEzBi-tamqgVCgAGraSsdTvqIrzlV115Lj_1IdtxqtemxEX1thv_YWAwMHy_q4GBX5OsunExMOzKet8NDGD7YC2hdb0ndNCha7aYbs9cSt6pNWgvV87lT9b_TnlE-A0AAP__S1tzHw) ahead of her reelection race. Arizona has 108 people on death row.
## Tucson Welcomes Home Honor Flight Veterans
Dozens of people [turned out at Tucson International Airport Thursday night](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OtCAYha8GO4z8CGNB8TV287VbGoQXJcuAwVfNztVvnFvY5hTnJE9Onq_n9LQxxbz8ty8waN9hynDtCRChTsHabDGWfEUPSy1H9juWbS0T77iijFEmJ-swnjBJ23gjlBu0bMAwPUilWC90s5qHdJ0GJ-Ywe5jDQ_FBzr5jUoZBD3puorl5jDHJRNcL2fpeAHto5ZQG1XNOZAc-YqktrmBrfJdsQ_opJ9TWlVeTzIq47UT8I3wkfLyuq_0uyd8j4eNNJ3xk7A7xKegJCNXmnVbAo2aKh9tLpjYgVLqWXCoNKS4rUqxxo94RPjbV-O2KKcVdaSK75WVj-hzAv7o7Df8NAAD__5nyg08) to cheer 20 Southern Arizona veterans home from a free Honor Flight trip to Washington, D.C. The group, made up of three Korean War veterans and 17 Vietnam veterans, [left Tuesday on Honor Flight Southern Arizona's 37th trip](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OnDAUBeCnMd1F-Ad7KCjS0G3alOhiXw_WGntk7oKyTx9NlDdIfaRP55xfH-sHppzK8yceNDN-x7XQfWZiprZGxIKcarlToGerXyWcXF97XdWgLEgJ0qzoOV20GuzCrK2fnOlolm4y1spRu26fBxxHL3V00W5bUG4iT3ajaMfH5Em7Ls1vT0pppB5GbfowapIPZ711ZEelhBkoJK6t552wpe9aMObf9aLW-3p0ed6ZX6fQP4RahFru--4_r4rvUKjlPUmoJVePWahFDXDWL96pFfiHwUVMDcsJjJ8ENUaoBfZaaoOY03Nn4AoBvFALNk4-06rtNJloDGyb9mAmNPCIzsK2xUFtQY0eVb_zkbs2h9edck6ndcIMzwNT_tub__fya1Z_AgAA__-qepZ3). They spent Veterans Day visiting the Vietnam Veterans Memorial Wall and the World War II, Korean War, and Lincoln memorials. When Vietnam veteran Bob Taylor came home decades ago, he and other service members [were chased through the Denver airport terminal](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OnDAUBeCnMZ0R_sEeChdp6DZtSnTX9zJYMTYyd0DZp48myhtsfaRP55xfH8sHpJzK8yfsFBi-1qXQfWZiprasAAU41XInpGerr4In12Orix60k0pJZReInC5aLHQYjIuTtx0F5SfrnBqN77YwqRWnhwO_Ooz-U5sY4wpjtGQ8OW-6FN6eUsoqM4zG9jgaUg_vovPkRq2FHQgT19bzRtDSVy2w5j_1otbHunc5bMzHKcwPoWeh5_u--99XhXco9PyeJPSca4Qs9HzWF2_UivwvyYv4lDflWHdCudWdJLDkVzxrkZDaURsLPUPjFDMtn_ahh2lEOaJGaa1FCQggo3cO3WOYImC_8Z67FvC4U87pdF7Y4blDyv8K83e_voL-GwAA__9gmJVK). _"This kind of takes the place of that, the welcome home we missed, so we really appreciate it, "_ Taylor said Thursday. After historic victories on Election Day, we were once again faced with the terrible reality of gun violence after the shooting in Washington DC this week.
#

Friend -
While I was having breakfast this morning, I found myself thinking of the GIFFORDS community and wanted to reach out to you personally.
After historic victories on Election Day, we were once again faced with the terrible reality of gun violence after the shooting in Washington DC this week. I think moments like this are worth reflecting on.
Over fifteen years ago, I was shot in the head while meeting with constituents in Tucson, Arizona. I've been in recovery every day since. Some days are harder than others. But even on the hardest days, I refuse to give up hope.
I think about our movement the same way. The work ahead isn't going to be easy. But the fights worth having rarely are.

Hi Advocate for Life, There is something beautiful about new life. Throughout creation, we see reminders of God's goodness, creativity, and care. But human life holds a uniquely sacred place. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: The Midterms – What to Make of Them?
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/midterms?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
So. Tariffs. Not so great, eh?

I think America has just given the world a pretty good demonstration of why tariffs are a very bad idea, both economically and politically.

Two years ago, Donald Trump was reelected, carrying every one of the swing states. He beat Kamala Harris, standing in for an administration widely blamed for soaring inflation and the rising cost of gas and groceries.

Yet within weeks of taking office, Trump slapped tariffs on Canada, Mexico and China, then on steel, aluminum and cars. On "Liberation Day" in April 2025, he hit almost every country, friend and foe alike, with tariffs of 10 to 50 per cent.

Tariffs, some said at the time, were all about taking on China. In which case, why, for heaven’s sake were they applied on imports from Canada?

Of course, it was neither Canadians nor Chinese that paid the tariffs. It was the American consumer. The National Taxpayers Union estimated a few months back that tariffs are costing US consumers around $200 billion a year. A basket of everyday back-to-school supplies is now $147 more expensive than before due to tariffs.

We know beyond doubt that tariffs were the key issue in the midterm election because the exit polls tell us so. Most voters said tariffs had hurt the economy. According to an NBC exit poll, about two thirds said the President’s policies had made it worse.

"But what about the Iran war?" some will ask. "Surely that played a part?"

It did, but it doesn't let tariffs off the hook. It made the damage worse. Launched with little thought for the consequences, the war choked off oil shipments from the Gulf for months. Gas prices soared, and so did the cost of essentials such as fertilizer. Voters already squeezed by tariffs were squeezed again.

No state shows more vividly the part tariffs played in the Republicans’ midterm disaster than our own. Mississippi has just gone and elected a Democrat to the Senate for the first time since 1982.

The defeated incumbent, Cindy Hyde-Smith, was an unequivocal champion of tariffs – at least initially. “I think that it’s a really good tool,” she once said. “The president knows how to use that tool.”

Her victorious opponent, Scott Colom, was anti-tariff — consistently, repeatedly and relentlessly. “The tariffs are a sales tax,” he told voters. “They’re a tax on everything.”

In Mississippi, the Democrat ran as a free trader — and won.

Most Americans – in this state and beyond - have worked out that tariffs make them poorer. If you still doubt it, stand in Kroger and admire one of those $20 bags of ground coffee. When I moved here six years ago, they cost around $11.

In the summer of 2025, Washington slapped a 50 percent tariff on Brazilian coffee. Who was it meant to protect? Mississippi has no coffee farmers. Apart from a handful of growers in Hawaii, neither does America. A little over three months later, the White House quietly dropped the tariff on coffee — which was as good as admitting that the tariff was being paid by ordinary American households.

Much of the damage done by tariffs could not so easily be undone. Mississippi’s soybean crop is worth around $1.6 billion a year, and almost all of it is sold abroad – at one time mostly to China.

When tariffs triggered a trade war, Beijing stopped buying American soybeans. It placed no orders for much of last year. Guess who filled the gap? Brazil. A market Mississippi farmers had spent decades building was handed to their biggest competitor. Even after a trade deal, China’s purchases are about half what they were.

It gets worse. That same summer, Washington put a 50 percent tariff on Brazilian beef, just as American beef prices were already soaring. The White House dropped that too within months – again an admission that it was American households paying. But the damage was done.

A pound of ground beef cost $6.76 last month. Five years ago, it was $4.72. “Shhhhiiiii”, one might say.
“Hold on!” I hear you wondering, “Why not feed our own soybeans to our own cattle, and stop relying on foreigners for either?”

Some 250 years ago, Adam Smith showed that nations grow rich by buying from others what those others make more cheaply. If that lesson has not yet reached policymakers, let me put it more bluntly.

Try telling a Mississippi mom at the checkout, worried if she’s enough on her card, that self-sufficiency is in the interests of her family, as you make her pay more for less. You might as well be telling her to go “pick another protein.”

To be fair to Cindy Hyde-Smith, she never actually said “pick another protein”, and in my view a fair amount of the campaign coverage was unfair to her.

When farmers complained about the cost of fertilizer, she went to the White House and fixed it by having the tariffs on it lifted. The same order also scrapped tariffs on beef and coffee.

But if tariffs are bad for Mississippi farmers when they buy fertilizer, why are they good for anyone else? It was another quiet admission of who pays — clear for anyone with eyes to see, long before election disaster the other day.

And it really was a disaster for the Republican Party. Texas has elected its first Democratic governor since 1990. Georgia elected Democrats to every statewide office. Kansas has sent a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in 94 years.

Democrats now hold at least 55 seats in the Senate. They are still short of the two thirds needed to override a presidential veto. Even so, I suspect that for the next two years it will often feel as if the Democrats are in power but not in office, while the Republicans are in office but not in power.

My greater fear, however, is that people will draw the wrong lessons.

Already there is pressure on the President to back off enforcing the law on illegal immigration. If the deportation agenda loses momentum, America risks starting to look like parts of Europe a few years down the line. A robust approach on immigration is the glue that has held the conservative coalition together. Go soft on that, and American conservatives will end up in as sorry a state as British ones.

I fear something similar regarding data centers. Republicans did badly despite being on the right side of that argument, not because of it. If the party now reads the result as a verdict against growth, it will throw away the one thing that can bring bills down — more investment, more jobs and more energy.

Voters did not reject conservatism. They rejected a tariff policy that made them poorer. The answer to that is not less free enterprise. It is more.

Perhaps there is one silver lining. Mississippi competes with other states for jobs, investment and people. If Texas and Georgia now choose to be governed like California, we have a chance to double down on a pro growth agenda.

Washington sets tariffs. Jackson can do a whole raft of things that make us more competitive. We cannot undo the damage done by bad federal policy, but we can make Mississippi the place where it pays to work, build and invest. Get rid of the income tax. Say yes to new investment. Go all in on affordable energy.

States that turn their backs on growth lose. Let’s make sure Mississippi is the one that gains.

name: Mary Peltola for Senate
subject: Overdrawn
body:
Peter --
As you read this, we basically have $0 in our bank account.
We are so grateful for this team for getting us to Election Day. Because of your support, Mary Peltola built this movement from the ground up without a dime from corporate special interests.
But now, this race still remains too close to call, and we could be waiting for results for a while.
We spent every dollar we had getting Mary across the finish line. Now that we’re in a holding pattern -- and with DC Republicans’ threats hanging over us -- we need to rebuild fast.
Since the beginning, Mary’s campaign has been powered by grassroots donation. We wish we didn’t need to keep asking after the election, but we need your support to keep pushing until this election is certified.
That’s why we have to ask:
**[Will you please split a donation between Mary Peltola’s campaign and Wes Moore to help make sure every vote is counted fairly? On Friday, October 23, 2026, federal prosecutors in Chicago announced that Parth Nayi, of Woodridge, had been sentenced to two years in prison and a $50,000 fine by U.S. District Judge Mary M. Rowland. Nayi pleaded guilty earlier this year to conspiracy to commit visa fraud. Prosecutors say he staged _hundreds_ of fake armed robberies across the country so that participants could claim to be crime victims on U-visa applications -- and that each participant paid him between $5,000 and $30,000 for the service (DOJ; FOX 32).
The scheme, step by step. The Chicago case broke open May 17, 2024, when prosecutors charged six men -- based in Woodridge, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, Wisconsin and Florida -- with staging holdups in and around the city; a June 2024 indictment listed robberies in Elmwood Park and River Grove (Tribune). The indictment catalogued more than a dozen venues: gas stations in Lombard and Hickory Hills; Subway restaurants in Chicago, Elmwood Park and Louisiana; a Tropical Smoothie Cafe in St. Charles; multiple Dunkin Donuts stores in Chicago and South Holland; liquor stores in Chicago, River Grove and Lake Villa; a 7-Eleven; a truck stop in Tennessee (CBS Chicago). body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.

| Letter from the Chair...
---
| Nebraska Republicans Delivered -- Now We Deliver for Them
Nebraska voters spoke clearly. We elected Republicans to every constitutional office and re-elected our incumbent members of Congress. We also secured a Republican majority on the State Board of Education. Where Republicans ran, we won more than 90 percent of the races.
We fell short in the open 2nd Congressional District seat and lost three seats in the Unicameral. In too many races, only a Democrat appeared on the ballot. Those gaps are real, and we have already begun the work to close them for 2028 at every level.
The election is over. The job of governing has begun.
Being in the minority in Congress is difficult, but difficulty is not an excuse. Democrats fought hard against a Republican majority; our voters expect the same tenacity from us. The same standard applies in Lincoln and in every county and school board. Voters will keep supporting us only if we show the will to fight for the things that matter to them: the right to worship according to conscience, the health and well-being of our families, the protection of our liberties, and the strength of our state and country.
At the NEGOP, that is the mindset we bring to work every morning--greater victories and measurable results. Every Republican should adopt it. Our values and the foundations of a free society are worth defending with energy and purpose. In the Unicameral, we must produce clear results. Democrats praise the "bipartisan" character of the body when it suits them, then campaign against Republicans as ineffective. We cannot give them that talking point. Our Governor has pledged courageous action; I take him at his word. Courage and boldness will be required to earn and keep the confidence of the people who elected us.
State Auditor Mike Foley demonstrated the kind of leadership that voters reward. He carried all 93 counties while pursuing waste, fraud, and abuse with integrity. Taxpayers notice when someone treats their money as something to be protected, not spent without accountability.
Our new Secretary of State, Scott Petersen, has committed to restoring and strengthening confidence in Nebraska's elections through greater transparency and accountability. That work is essential and has already begun.
Nebraska Republicans understand that we will not win every race. What they will not accept is the appearance that we failed to give our best effort. The opportunity to prove ourselves starts every morning. Let's meet it.
Forward.
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

Thank You, Ramona Christian Won!
---
| | |
---
Fellow Republicans of the 5th District,

I'm thrilled to share that Ramona Christian has been elected Chair of the 5th Congressional District Republican Committee.

This is a great day for our district. Ramona brings energy, organization, and a proven record of getting results. She worked tirelessly helping us win a 5th District race that even Democrats admitted they couldn't believe we won. She knows every corner of the 5th, she knows how to build relationships, and she is ready on day one to grow our party and help turn Virginia red again.

I want to thank every delegate who showed up, stood strong, and voted for real leadership. Your presence and your voices mattered.

Now the real work begins. FYI my democrat opponent Tom Perriello has made it clear he plans to run against me again in 2028 and he is already campaigning around the district.

The distractions and division in our party need to end. No more internal games and retribution. Our focus must be on defeating the radical Democrat agenda, supporting our republican candidates, and building a stronger Republican Party across the 5th District and our commonwealth

Congratulations, Ramona. I look forward to working with you as our new District Chair.

name: James Talarico
subject: Go big or go home
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Talarico for Texas
body:
#
Peter —
As I walked the halls of the United States Senate during our orientation earlier this week, Lyndon B. Johnson was everywhere — busts, portraits, plaques. It felt like he was speaking to me as I prepared to take back his Senate seat.
I think LBJ has something to say to all of us in this moment.
LBJ married two things that are at odds in the modern Democratic Party: the practical politics of coalition-building and a bold moral imagination.
LBJ’s Great Society was not just a legislative agenda; it was a vision. It was a dream. An America where everyone can fulfill their God-given potential. A beloved community. A more perfect union.
And he passed an agenda worthy of that dream: Head Start, Title 1, Medicare, Medicaid, public television, the Civil Rights Act, the Voting Rights Act, fair housing, space exploration, the War on Poverty, the National Endowment for the Arts, highway beautification.
Everything is bigger in Texas — including our policy ambitions. In Texas, we go big, or we go home.
So here’s what I told Democrats gathered for a post-midterm debrief about we need to do with our Texas-sized mandate:
* We must get Big Money out of our politics so no billionaire — or trillionaire — can buy our elections.
* We must ban gerrymandering nationwide — in red states and blue states alike.
* We must unrig this economic system that only benefits the top 1%.
* We must pass universal healthcare so no one goes bankrupt just because they get sick.
* We must invest in our teachers and our students and build an American public education system that is the envy of the world.
* We must overhaul this broken immigration system and build a pathway to citizenship for our neighbors who have been here for years.
* We must cut red tape and build millions of new homes so every American can realize the dream of homeownership.
* We must regulate artificial intelligence, crack down on data centers, and pass an AI Dividend so every American has a share in this AI future.
* We must end these forever wars that are driving up prices and champion a new, values-based foreign policy.

As we look ahead to January, as we look ahead to the next couple of years, we need to summon the ambition of LBJ.
The American people want change, and in this election, they gave our party a chance to deliver it.
We can’t let them down.
We can’t play it safe.
We can’t get bogged down in petty fights.
We can’t settle for nibbling around the edges or results people will only feel a decade from now.
We need to be brave. We need to be bold. We need to be big. We need a Democratic Party that’s a little less Washington, and a little more Texas.
In the words of Thomas Paine: “We have it in our power to begin the world over again."
We can write the next chapter of our history. We can remake our country. We can build a new Great Society.
It’s time to go big or go home.
James
The fights ahead will not be easy. Billionaires and corporate interests spent record-breaking sums to try to defeat our movement in Texas. The status quo is not done fighting back to keep the system rigged.
**[If we are going to pass our agenda in the U.S. Senate and continue to win in Texas, then James will need all of us to have his back. We spent down to zero to win Texas, so please consider making a contribution to support our people-powered movement.](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261114-1-ak&t=1&akid=1192%2E1347274%2EZtuP_8)**
[CONTRIBUTE](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261114-1-ak&t=2&akid=1192%2E1347274%2EZtuP_8)

name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
subject: How we did it (again)
body:
|
#
Friend, Two years ago, we won a district President Trump carried by 2 points. When people asked how we did it, I told them the answer was simple: we did things differently. Well, we did it again this election. And the answer hasn’t changed. **Here’s what you need to know:**
* We won by 14 points in one of the most competitive districts in the country – despite millions in outside spending.
* Our campaign showed the strongest crossover appeal of any Democratic House candidate in Michigan.
* Every corner of this district moved our way compared to 2024: Flint, Saginaw, Bay City, and Midland too.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143450217/660253151/-185804088?refcode=em-11.14.26-all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZjlkOGQ2MC00MmUwLWYxMTEtOTFmMC0wMDBkM2ExOGUyNDQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VyhIBI3sP8SXq1jx1IqpekkjQi0CY0jgsUhRrNfmD-4=) None of that happened by accident, friend. Our team spent this cycle on front porches all across the district – in fact, we knocked on 200,000 doors. We talked about what people here actually lose sleep over: being able to work one job and build a middle-class life, the cost of child care and prescription drugs, and protecting fundamental rights. And in this election, voters could see what I’d done in Congress. When Elon Musk tried to shut down Saginaw’s Social Security office, we rallied the community and saved it. Working families on SNAP still can’t buy a hot rotisserie chicken at the grocery store, so I got a bill through the House to change that – and I won’t stop until it’s law. Two years ago, I said I wasn’t going to play by Washington’s rules. I meant it. And mid-Michigan noticed. Now, with a Democratic majority, we finally have the chance to deliver on more of what voters have been asking for: lower costs, affordable health care, and a government that works for _you,_ not special interests. More soon, Kristen | ** 👋 Before you go...** Holding this seat wasn’t cheap. Outside groups poured millions into trying to defeat us, and we had to spend big to fight back. Unfortunately, we expect Republicans to make this one of their top targets again in 2028.

subject: Federal Judge Rules Religious Discrimination Against Christians Still Illegal in Maine
body:
