A federal judge ruled Friday that the Hermon School Department violated The Pines Church's rights under the First Amendment and the Maine Human Rights Act when it denied the church a year-long lease of school facilities.
Chief U.S. District Judge Lance E. Walker issued the [37-page Decision and Order](https://substack.com/redirect/948b7072-3a6e-4667-aff9-7ea9f931b544?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after a two-day bench trial in the lawsuit brought by the church and its lead pastor, Matt Gioia. Walker entered a declaratory judgment that the department's treatment and denial of the church's application for a year-long lease violated those rights.
The Maine Wire first broke the story about the discriminatory actions of the Hermon School Department -- and ex-school board member Christopher McLaughlin, in particular -- back in 2023 when it obtained emails via the Freedom of Access Act showing McLaughlin attempting to impose a religious litmus test on who would be allowed to rent public spaces controlled by the school system.
You can count on the liberal media to expose stories like this. Or you can support The Robinson Report.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..TjTTMghB9fQ9F5Kk75TEYgRay36HdxcCda5HHKyY5qo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=224822561)
In response to the Christian church's request to rent the school gymnasium, McLaughlin sent an email to Superintendent Micah Grant demanding that Gioia explain what the church teaches about transvestites, whether boys can become girls, abortion, birth control, and genital mutilation for young people.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d232c8db-854d-488a-bbcc-567b00541baf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The obvious implication of McLaughlin's email was that if the Christian pastor taught Christian beliefs at his Christian church, then McLaughlin would use his position of power to discriminate against the lease request on the basis of those religious beliefs.
He resigned in 2024 when Pines Church sued over the attempted religious discrimination. Two years later, the blatant act of anti-Christian bigotry has finally been confirmed by a federal judge.
Walker found it more likely than not that "discriminatory animus toward the Church" motivated the department to decline the year-long lease. Under the Maine Human Rights Act, he found that "the Church's status was a substantial factor in the Committee's decision not to lease to the Church for their requested lease term." He wrote of "undertones and overtones of bad motive unabated throughout the decision-making process."
McLaughlin has previously served as the Associate Vice President of Community and Pediatric Services at Northern Light Acadia Hospital in Bangor and Executive Director of the National Association of Social Workers (NASW) Maine Chapter. He has also served on the Maine Board of Social Work Licensing and on boards for the Maine Children's Alliance and a Diversity Hiring Coalition.
Although Walker ruled in favor of Pines Church, he denied the church's request for an injunction. He awarded the church and Gioia $1 in nominal damages (court-ordered) and reasonable costs. Attorney fees have not yet been determined.
At its December 12, 2022, meeting, the Hermon School Committee did not take a vote on the church's request for a year-long lease of the theater, cafeteria and classrooms at Hermon High School for Sunday morning services. Vice Chair Shorey moved a six-month lease. The motion failed for lack of a second. Member Stephanie Oiler then moved a month-to-month lease, which passed 4-1. Chair Jesse Keith, Shorey, Oiler and Haily Keezer voted yes. Christopher McLaughlin voted no.
Gioia rejected the month-to-month offer, as he'd previously explained to the board that a month-to-month arrangement was not tenable for the church's long-term planning. Conservative critics at the time called the purported compromise a bad-faith attempt to cover up for McLaughlin's outed animus.
Walker agreed. He wrote that the committee knew the church needed a more fixed arrangement, and that the month-to-month offer "appears to me to have been an offer designed to be rejected not one born of wholesome support for the Free Exercise Clause." He did not order the department to grant a longer lease.
Walker found that at least three of the committee's five voting members acted under the influence of bad motive: McLaughlin, Oiler and Shorey.
He wrote, "I find without any difficulty that McLaughlin exhibited bad motive," and that McLaughlin's "intrusive questions expressed viewpoint related concerns towards Plaintiffs."
In addition to the questions McLaughlin put in writing to the superintendent, the LGBTQ activist also interrogated Gioia at an in-person meeting. At the church's November 7, 2022, presentation, McLaughlin asked about the church's denomination.
Grant forwarded the questions to Gioia on November 10.
Gioia did not answer them.
Instead, he responded in a November 28 letter that it is "entirely inappropriate for a representative of the State (the school board) to ask a religious organization about their faith, morality, and political stances, when considering them for a lease or for any other matter."
Oiler raised concerns about crowd size, parking, staffing and cleaning. Walker wrote that the members' concerns were "definitively dispelled" by Grant, and that "Oiler's attitude toward the Church was anything but neutral." He found that "Oiler's chief concern was that the tenant would be a Church."
Walker credited Grant, who testified that he is a born-again Christian, with "acting as a guardrail" when the committee "started to drive the process into a constitutional bridge abutment." He wrote that "Grant's conduct as to procedure supported and favored treating the Church equally to all other potential public users of public space."
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack.com/redirect/d02501dd-83ee-44e4-8fd7-e5167ef223b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Grant announced his [resignation in April 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/e0f16e40-dcee-4374-830c-82053be8c926?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), citing personal reasons.
The department has said the church was treated like other community groups. Its attorney, Melissa Hewey of far-left law firm Drummond Woodsum, argued at a June 2024 hearing that the church was allowed to use the facility and simply was not granted a year-long lease. The opinion records Grant telling the committee that this was the first year-long lease request it had received. Walker wrote that "novelty is not a basis to discriminate against religious organizations."
McLaughlin, Oiler and Shorey -- the three school board members found to have acted out of bad-faith animus toward Christians -- won't suffer any financial penalty for the attempted discrimination, as the taxpayers cover the costs of Drummond Woodsum's LGBTQ advocacy in schools.
The Pines Church case is oddly similar to another instance of anti-Christian bigotry from a separate taxpayer-funded institution: the University of Maine System.
[[RELATED: UMaine Rescinds Offer to Sell Hutchinson Center to Belfast Church...]](https://substack.com/redirect/d5d36a96-6c7f-489e-b85a-f531d25d6eff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In 2024, after Calvary Chapel Belfast won the bid to purchase the system's Hutchinson Center to serve as its new church, UMS caved to pressure from left-wing activists and [reneged](https://substack.com/redirect/d5d36a96-6c7f-489e-b85a-f531d25d6eff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the sale.

Folks, One year ago, electing and re-electing Democratic Secretaries of State was going to be a difficult feat. Trump and MAGA Republicans had full control over our democracy. But thanks to your support, we elected four Secretaries in crucial battleground states: **Nevada’s Cisco Aguilar, Arizona’s Adrian Fontes, Michigan’s Garlin Gilchrist, and Georgia's Penny Brown Reynolds.** We also have new Democratic Secretaries of State in Indiana and Ohio – **thanks to Beau Bayh and Allison Russo.** | [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143451230/660257186/-248329301?refcode=em-11.14.26-all-1-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZjcxMjI3OC00NGUwLWYxMTEtOTFmMC0wMDBkM2ExOGUyNDQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=8cswMj2_SA9sLX6jAXsdAZQb8u35yiuXULn4ZXGThMU=) **“Democrats will oversee future elections in four presidential swing states after they made inroads in traditionally red states.”**
---
Secretaries of State have always done the essential work of democracy: certifying results, protecting voter rolls, and making sure every eligible vote counts. Now that Trump is working to sow distrust in our elections, that work is a critical backstop against his chaos.
[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143451231/660257187/-248329301?refcode=em-11.14.26-all-1-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZjcxMjI3OC00NGUwLWYxMTEtOTFmMC0wMDBkM2ExOGUyNDQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=8cswMj2_SA9sLX6jAXsdAZQb8u35yiuXULn4ZXGThMU=) **“Starting in 2027, the [Democratic] party will run, or have the ability to choose who runs, at least 21 state election offices... the Secretary of State can be quite influential in how elections are administered.”**
---
Democrats now oversee elections in more states than before. That’s exactly why Trump keeps trying to discredit them: if he can’t win the count, he’ll try to undermine undermine the results.
He’s reviving outlandish theories about our voting machines being rigged rather than believing the American people don’t want their voting rights being attacked.
Our current and new Democratic Secretaries of State will work tirelessly to protect each ballot that was cast and do everything in their power to keep our elections free, fair and secure.

clean_body: | ~ | | Peter, I understand that organizers don’t have unlimited resources. I understand that sometimes, we have to make tough calls. I understand that big dreams take time to achieve. But I will never understand how anyone could look me in the eyes and tell me that my home state – and everyone living there – isn’t “worth” fighting for. Still, people always ask why we’re so invested in organizing across Florida. They claim that Florida is too red, too far gone, too deep under the thumb of the far-right fascists like Ron DeSantis, and that we can’t “afford” to fight back. If I’d listened to that kind of defeatism in 2022, I wouldn’t be writing to you today as the first Gen Z member of Congress. And I’m damn sure not listening to it in 2026. ~ | | ~ Thanks to people like you, chipping in spare change and sometimes digging even deeper, we’ve gained ground in Florida. This state is in play, and you won’t catch me on the sidelines when everything from our education to our democracy to our planet’s survival is at stake. Now, I’m not gonna sugarcoat what we’re really up against. It’s true that Floridians have been subjected to far-right policies for years, and that it’s caused real suffering. It’s true that billionaire weirdos have been funding fascism here for even longer. But that’s exactly why we have to organize and fight back. Friend, my message to party leadership is simple: Don’t just talk about a majority, show us what a majority can do. Don’t just talk about healthcare justice, pass Medicare for All. Don’t just talk about abortion justice, pass national abortion protections. Don’t just talk about Black lives mattering, enact reparations now. Don’t just talk about ending ICE’s terror, take every last dollar from them and abolish ICE. We have the power, and now we have to actually use it. **This is all possible with our hard-fought victories. And we owe it to voters to deliver.** Now is not the time to moderate our aspirations. # How to Unsend an Email on iPhone After You’ve Sent It
Have you ever tapped send and immediately realized something was wrong with your email? We've all been there. You can unsend an email on your iPhone or iPad if you realize your mistake within a set amount of time. This can save you a lot of embarrassment and the pain of having to write a follow-up correction email.
## Why You’ll Love This Tip
* **Learn how to take back an email you wish you hadn’t sent.**
* **Avoid conflict, confusion, or embarrassment by unsending emails.**
* **Change the timeframe you have to unsend emails, from 10 seconds up to 30 seconds.**

## How to Recall and Email Sent on iPhone & iPad
### System Requirements
_This tip works on iPhones running iOS 16 or later, and was tested on an iPhone 17 Pro running iOS 26.4. Find out how to update to[the latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-260936-8633304-eb261b4cda-ejbc834839)._If you change your mind after tapping send on an email, you can unsend the email on your iPad or iPhone. If you wish to unsend an email that you sent via the Mail app, you have [up to 30 seconds](href=) to do so.Note: If you delete an email, does it unsend? The answer is no. The recipient still receives and keeps the email even if you delete it on your end. Using the Undo Send Delay feature is the only way to recall an email sent once you've hit the send icon.
1. Open the **Mail app** on your iPhone.

|
---
2. Draft an email and select a recipient, then tap the **Send icon**.

---
3. Tap the **Undo Send button** at the top of the Inbox to stop the email from sending.

---
### Enjoying Your Tip of the Day?
If you'd like to learn more about iPhone Life's premium paid subscription, [click here](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-260936-8633305-2dbe5f5e1d-ejbc834839)

After you stop the email from sending, your Mail app will open the draft again, so you can edit it and resend if necessary.
If you wait longer than 10 seconds, you won’t be able to unsend the email unless you change the Mail Undo Send Delay in your settings. You can unsend an email regardless of whether the recipient has an iPhone or is running the latest software.
### How to Change the Mail Undo Send Delay Time
If you’d like to give yourself some more time to unsend an email, you can do so in the settings:
1. Open the **Settings app.**

---
2. Tap **Apps.**

---
3. Tap **Mail**.

---
4. Scroll to the bottom and tap **Undo Send Delay**.

---
5. Here you can pick between Off, 10 Seconds, 20 Seconds, and 30 Seconds. Tap one to select it.

---

I like to set my unsend email time limit to 30 seconds because it usually takes me a while to realize I made a mistake, so the more time I have, the better. name: Save the Persecuted Christians
subject: A little Christian girl urgently needs your help
body:
We wish we could tell you Silvia's story is rare. It isn't.
| [](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=56e22257159f419d848491e1b5da4a9d&_e=e3q805OvDjsQLSZtmIsnOGQZlW4pB6-ok-luRpbnOi6mixhq6ooi-abtpMtUR-_DaO2x9O_Z6iAvCt83B5OXQC-SE-0s0s2qcG4dxvMfvHSVfX5_9lVYYlu8YzGTm31avsTlgn_VtcU33RO7XkZj30mS6TGmBIZELD0NmENUANmSdL0sAJyw0eI7G9DWWOj54ViZxZYAhCRDj8mLl0mShqIh1JzYwdhRF5w7E0nxurNbM03mmTX_GFYAwiq3nK3LW2HiLahR9SVuPfMmcTju3rtGkHPcQx_aw6tbp9myrtTmfyvuyWxUsUPy-E0Lw6N_lU3bkIxMt730Yp6ma-MC5H-3HrCb61rlI5PJaKzmMfewzOteOMIuEiWMfQvcn_j_hBxJWR6WIYpIibjLo6YQ9bI0GgLR4J9ftk6CY_U3XTjGIRlN7obabreh7Pm--y6RQ87PxiwNStY5pPh3bdWoOuwcMEUXNY2bSN9ODYsMyZaJhCX99nSabLF_w-fwLTMeuT3GrIidCPmuAUT6-LhYgBMhtOBqocP77ny0IXiwSLq6awKdLvcSf4mnviArh_9SsQMW_xoT_dz-1fM7LwFF8SwWrGFCLZyWW2AA-0Kj8L7O6E1eW9ZHVXvuszdE1JyWxKY5xN6NEWIT4M2OnbJQdFkDeuiG_qvLsQ0XzYbMe2Nn29y38rPRmd6k2ICzmM7jPOGqf2plpk3573zUFvoJSrGFbOMPVRv6ddJPwW9MJfeSj76gktG_IyYUEO8E7qt5x-mzbXxsdHzCNw0tBu6dm5qiDU33cCb-xo7DqRsG41PquEoHgrpIlOQzzQCwyP3TsgrytdALUr4Gb8-NMBoOyUuUlja3z0aZXcxGSxImrdM%3D)
---
Dear Faithful Friend,
Some stories are hard to read. Silvia's is one of them. But we are asking you to read it, because she needs people who will not look away – and she needs them today.
Silvia Samuel is a little girl from Awon, a small village in northern Nigeria. It's a largely Christian area that has been hit again and again by attacks and kidnappings.
On the morning of April 20, armed men stormed Awon. Eleven people were taken.
**Among them were three-year-old Silvia and her mother, Joy, who was pregnant.**
They were dragged to a forest camp – the same camp where, just two weeks earlier, kidnappers had held worshippers seized from Easter Sunday church services nearby.
In captivity, Joy gave birth with no help. Her newborn baby died.
Then Joy died too.
Silvia was left alone in the hands of her captors. She turned four in that camp. At one point, the people praying for her feared she had died as well.
Five of the eleven taken from Awon died in captivity, including two young children.
**In early November, Silvia was finally freed. But she came home without her mother. And she came home critically ill.**
We wish we could tell you Silvia's story is rare. It isn't.
Nigeria is now the deadliest country on earth for Christians. Open Doors found that 3,490 of the 4,849 Christians killed for their faith worldwide in its latest count were Nigerian – more than every other country combined. And this year, at least 3,083 more were killed in just eight months, according to the rights group Intersociety.
Villages burned. Churches emptied. Children taken.
**This is a genocide. And we 'll be honest with you: we cannot stop a tragedy this massive by ourselves.** No ministry can. No single donor can.
**But for this one little girl, we can do something real – right now.**
Silvia lies in a small local hospital. Her father, who has already lost his wife and his newborn child, has been trying to raise the money to move her to a better hospital in the city.
[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=56e22257159f419d848491e1b5da4a9d&_e=e3q805OvDjsQLSZtmIsnOGQZlW4pB6-ok-luRpbnOi6mixhq6ooi-abtpMtUR-_DaO2x9O_Z6iAvCt83B5OXQC-SE-0s0s2qcG4dxvMfvHSVfX5_9lVYYlu8YzGTm31avsTlgn_VtcU33RO7XkZj30mS6TGmBIZELD0NmENUANmSdL0sAJyw0eI7G9DWWOj54ViZxZYAhCRDj8mLl0mShqIh1JzYwdhRF5w7E0nxurNbM03mmTX_GFYAwiq3nK3LW2HiLahR9SVuPfMmcTju3rtGkHPcQx_aw6tbp9myrtTmfyvuyWxUsUPy-E0Lw6N_o-hyTg4iQ-6mcMt8Xp_52MNuihdGTmRKU8Z8kifK84NI0nlzvMkXGWA0VfcIfmuIEXpI1SojwcoRBDyi_lPP_i5HiEo1rddUr9UpKYe4St6fnD3dBjO3TIEL118vki8Dqk5SfZJYqmBAydyO37DSsAbH2z5tdeEA84ZXG4F9dCuuXHo4h1pEp69g7VBqDZMVtQ9KUP7GK-yfnF7Z-FEj2xmhXWz6XouI80HA24QIlPIwykwxHwK-E-5vQQGz1tzMp3r9mGJLJ9QEHmtKF_ISxvCqnbUzZnCBRatOvXIEtTBnawBF5Smu2uJ3KP4Tv5J-DCuIUx7XgAJ6ug9j-XpE_72uORmBgf005Rl_-9tDtqcQZ_4xpGqzIu2gKR5wpOp7gr6BeShNEM_7TplYl3SXM111u-yUB0BZf_3Jd0dlxTVhkdHEnkWE-MhU2loKrkaH1uysptuSqLIHIBmlc5Mb9X99QJIrEa0j2RXrQNEANFbsadmd-aG0ooxzPYE3UXQzE9xiNFU1XilPmTy4d6XYFZu4PIunLD5FU4zDgaWcc2g%3D)
Stop and picture that father at her bedside. He has already buried too much. **Now he is fighting to keep his little girl alive.** He should not have to fight alone.
Jesus said that _whatever we do for the least of these, we do for Him._ Silvia cannot speak for herself. She cannot pay for her own care. But we can stand with her.

clean_body: We wish we could tell you Silvia's story is rare. It isn't. | Dear Faithful Friend, Some stories are hard to read. Silvia's is one of them. But we are asking you to read it, because she needs people who will not look away – and she needs them today. Silvia Samuel is a little girl from Awon, a small village in northern Nigeria. It's a largely Christian area that has been hit again and again by attacks and kidnappings. On the morning of April 20, armed men stormed Awon. Eleven people were taken. Among them were three-year-old Silvia and her mother, Joy, who was pregnant. They were dragged to a forest camp – the same camp where, just two weeks earlier, kidnappers had held worshippers seized from Easter Sunday church services nearby. In captivity, Joy gave birth with no help. Her newborn baby died. Then Joy died too. Silvia was left alone in the hands of her captors. She turned four in that camp. At one point, the people praying for her feared she had died as well. Five of the eleven taken from Awon died in captivity, including two young children. In early November, Silvia was finally freed. But she came home without her mother. And she came home critically ill. We wish we could tell you Silvia's story is rare. It isn't. Nigeria is now the deadliest country on earth for Christians. Open Doors found that 3,490 of the 4,849 Christians killed for their faith worldwide in its latest count were Nigerian – more than every other country combined. And this year, at least 3,083 more were killed in just eight months, according to the rights group Intersociety. Villages burned. Churches emptied. Children taken. This is a genocide. And we 'll be honest with you: we cannot stop a tragedy this massive by ourselves. No ministry can. No single donor can. But for this one little girl, we can do something real – right now. Silvia lies in a small local hospital. Her father, who has already lost his wife and his newborn child, has been trying to raise the money to move her to a better hospital in the city. Stop and picture that father at her bedside. He has already buried too much. Now he is fighting to keep his little girl alive. He should not have to fight alone. * * *
I'm writing this from the Denver airport, where I'm desperately trying to get home to my family after this debacle, a nationwide ground stop courtesy of the Trump administration. I'm working through my options, and mostly I'm just sitting here stewing with rage. I'm probably not going to make it home today to hang out with my son, and that's what I've been looking forward to all week.
And I keep thinking about everyone else stuck in this mess. The people trying to get to weddings. To funerals. To the bedside of a sick loved one. This is exactly why it matters that we have a functioning government full of actual public servants who know what the fuck they're doing.
Instead, we have a Secretary of Transportation whose main qualification is he was on a reality TV show and Trump thinks he looks good on TV. Everything about this was preventable.
They spent the last two years screaming about DEI and purging qualified people from the government, people who actually knew what they were doing. So now we don't just have one Sean Duffy at the Department of Transportation, or one Pete Hegseth at the Department of Defense, or one Kash Patel at the FBI. We have thousands of them. They're all over the government, and they're ruining this country in big ways, like what happened yesterday, and in small ways that materially make your life worse.
I don't believe a single word coming out of Markwayne Mullin's or Sean Duffy's unqualified, idiotic mouths about this, because they lie about everything. I'm not going to pretend I know exactly what happened. Maybe it was the AI system. Maybe it was some other update, or a cyberattack, or God knows what. But I know I don't trust these people.
We're essentially governed by people who don't believe there should be a government. So I'm assuming some of this ends with Republicans like Duffy pushing to privatize air traffic control, which they've floated before, because everything they do has to have a grift at the end of it. And if I had to guess, we'll eventually find out these people are profiteering off this whole mess, too.
Like how Sean Duffy's goofy son-in-law with the eyebrows apparently works for the AI company that pushed the update that may have caused this entire debacle.

* * *
Last week, voters told these people exactly what they thought of this. They clearly weren't listening.
What gets me is how insidious it is. Their incompetence betrays the very people they claim to represent. It seeps into everything and makes our day-to-day lives that much worse.
Look, on some level, it's the little things that get you through the day. I've had a long week on the road at a conference here in Denver, and it was great. I got to spend time with a lot of people I love, do some networking, and meet with some great political candidates. But by the end of the week I was running on fumes, and what kept me going was the weekend. Couch. College football. My people.
Instead, I'm stuck here, because the government can't keep the goddamn planes in the sky.
Once again, this administration's material incompetence and corruption has made my life worse, and very likely made your life worse too. Not to mention whatever damage this is doing to the economy. And they don't care. I guarantee you Sean Duffy slept like a baby last night. I guarantee you Markwayne Mullin slept like a fucking baby last night. They do not care how their incompetence hurts the American people. They simply don't.
Yesterday, Sean Duffy was out there saying Congress needs to step in and fix this, and that they've got to give him more money. He said it just like that: give me the money. Not "invest in fixing the problem." Give it to _him_. A man whose only qualification for this job is that Donald Trump thought he looked good on TV because he was on _The Real World_. A man who spent a bunch of time whoring himself out to different companies to get a stupid documentary about himself made.
I'm not surprised. But I remain flabbergasted and outraged by these people.
I wouldn't give any of them one single fucking dime until, at minimum, Trump fires Sean Duffy and appoints a Transportation Secretary who knows what the hell they're doing. Maybe we can get Mayor Pete back, because this shit didn't happen on his watch.
The government's job isn't complicated. Keep the planes in the sky. Make sure our food doesn't make us sick. Keep us safe. Keep the economy functioning. Don't, I don't know, blow up the global energy market because of a stupid war. I don't think any of these are unreasonable things to ask.
So here I am, steaming mad in this unruly, gangly mess of an airport, trying to figure out how to get home to my wife and son. That's all I want today. I don't know if I'm going to make it, and that fucking sucks.
And I know a lot of people out there have it worse than I do. So if you're traveling today, be safe and stay calm. I love you, and I hope you get where you need to go as quickly as possible.
With urgency,
--Mike

I'm writing this from the Denver airport, where I'm desperately trying to get home to my family after this debacle, a nationwide ground stop courtesy of the Trump administration. I'm working through my options, and mostly I'm just sitting here stewing with rage. I'm probably not going to make it home today to hang out with my son, and that's what I've been looking forward to all week. And I keep thinking about everyone else stuck in this mess. The people trying to get to weddings. To funerals. To the bedside of a sick loved one. This is exactly why it matters that we have a functioning government full of actual public servants who know what the fuck they're doing. Instead, we have a Secretary of Transportation whose main qualification is he was on a reality TV show and Trump thinks he looks good on TV. Everything about this was preventable. They spent the last two years screaming about DEI and purging qualified people from the government, people who actually knew what they were doing. So now we don't just have one Sean Duffy at the Department of Transportation, or one Pete Hegseth at the Department of Defense, or one Kash Patel at the FBI. We have thousands of them. They're all over the government, and they're ruining this country in big ways, like what happened yesterday, and in small ways that materially make your life worse. I don't believe a single word coming out of Markwayne Mullin's or Sean Duffy's unqualified, idiotic mouths about this, because they lie about everything. I'm not going to pretend I know exactly what happened. Maybe it was the AI system. Maybe it was some other update, or a cyberattack, or God knows what. But I know I don't trust these people. We're essentially governed by people who don't believe there should be a government. So I'm assuming some of this ends with Republicans like Duffy pushing to privatize air traffic control, which they've floated before, because everything they do has to have a grift at the end of it. And if I had to guess, we'll eventually find out these people are profiteering off this whole mess, too. Like how Sean Duffy's goofy son-in-law with the eyebrows apparently works for the AI company that pushed the update that may have caused this entire debacle. * Last week, voters told these people exactly what they thought of this. They clearly weren't listening. What gets me is how insidious it is. Their incompetence betrays the very people they claim to represent. It seeps into everything and makes our day-to-day lives that much worse. Look, on some level, it's the little things that get you through the day. I've had a long week on the road at a conference here in Denver, and it was great. I got to spend time with a lot of people I love, do some networking, and meet with some great political candidates. But by the end of the week I was running on fumes, and what kept me going was the weekend. Couch. College football. My people. Instead, I'm stuck here, because the government can't keep the goddamn planes in the sky. Once again, this administration's material incompetence and corruption has made my life worse, and very likely made your life worse too. Not to mention whatever damage this is doing to the economy. And they don't care. I guarantee you Sean Duffy slept like a baby last night. I guarantee you Markwayne Mullin slept like a fucking baby last night. They do not care how their incompetence hurts the American people. They simply don't. Yesterday, Sean Duffy was out there saying Congress needs to step in and fix this, and that they've got to give him more money. He said it just like that: give me the money. Not "invest in fixing the problem." Give it to him. A man whose only qualification for this job is that Donald Trump thought he looked good on TV because he was on The Real World. A man who spent a bunch of time whoring himself out to different companies to get a stupid documentary about himself made. I'm not surprised. But I remain flabbergasted and outraged by these people. I wouldn't give any of them one single fucking dime until, at minimum, Trump fires Sean Duffy and appoints a Transportation Secretary who knows what the hell they're doing. Maybe we can get Mayor Pete back, because this shit didn't happen on his watch. The government's job isn't complicated. Keep the planes in the sky. Make sure our food doesn't make us sick. Keep us safe. Keep the economy functioning. Don't, I don't know, blow up the global energy market because of a stupid war. I don't think any of these are unreasonable things to ask. So here I am, steaming mad in this unruly, gangly mess of an airport, trying to figure out how to get home to my wife and son. That's all I want today. I don't know if I'm going to make it, and that fucking sucks. And I know a lot of people out there have it worse than I do. So if you're traveling today, be safe and stay calm. I love you, and I hope you get where you need to go as quickly as possible. #### ** Everything is Bigger in Texas,
Even Election History**
---
|
---
| Friends,

This cycle, we had the privilege of bringing candidates’ messages to life in English and Spanish—connecting the economic pressures families face with the failures of Republican leadership and a clear alternative. Here are a few examples of creative that broke through:
**Texas Governor: Gina Hinojosa**
In "No Te Dejes," produced for Somos PAC, we spoke directly to Texas families facing rising energy costs while Greg Abbott handed billions in tax incentives to data centers.

**"No Te Dejes," ran by Somos PAC**
| **TX-15: Bobby Pulido**
These ads held Monica De La Cruz accountable for supporting a budget that cut Medicaid in one of the nation’s poorest districts, while showing why Texans need a fighter like Bobby Pulido.

| **CO-08: Manny Rutinel**
Our digital ads and DCCC mailer put Manny Rutinel’s record side by side with Gabe Evans’s votes supporting Trump’s Iran war while diesel prices topped $6 a gallon in Colorado.

**Mailer ran by the DCCC**
| **AZ-06: JoAnna Mendoza**
In “Elegimos,” produced for House Majority PAC, and in a mailer for Unidos Action Fund, we highlighted Juan Ciscomani’s broken promises and how his votes on tariffs and health care left Arizonans footing the bill.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/GzPCEpkcV2S?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)

**Mailer ran by Unidos Action Fund **
| **CA-48: Marni Von Wilpert**
Our Spanish-language ads for House Majority PAC contrasted Marni’s career holding price-gouging corporations accountable with Jim Desmond’s record.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/yQ5FXmtQwyJ?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)

Friend, with massive Democratic majorities incoming in Congress, there are so many possibilities on the table.
The American people have given us a historic task: Rein in this runaway president, end his stupid war, bring down costs, and root out the rampant corruption and oligarchy that has held our government and economy captive. But with so much to do, we need to focus our efforts.
So, I want to hear from you directly. [**What do you want me, my team, and our movement to do first in the new Congress? Click the button below to chime in:**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-nov26-issues-survey/?source=em261114-1-180&refcode2=2598.791427._am1TY&akid=2598%2E791427%2E_am1TY)

Grassroots organizing is how we won these majorities, and grassroots organizing **must** be how we pursue our agenda.
That’s because it’s not politicians like me who make progress in our democracy. It’s the millions of dedicated people who drive movements for change, pushing the politicians to do the right thing and respond to the will of the People.
These majorities would not have been won without the dedication of everyone who showed up, protested, organized, donated, knocked doors, made phone calls, talked to their neighbors, and pressured their elected officials over the last two years.
So whether your top priority is fixing the GOP’s healthcare disaster, ending endless wars, or putting a stop to ICE violence across the country, I want to make sure EVERYONE’s voice is heard as we transition into this exciting and historic moment.

In solidarity,
Ilhan Omar

body:
Families are being torn apart without due process, and kids are paying the price.
#
**We need your help to speak out against the imprisonment of children in detention centers, Peter.**
In Maryland, 19-year-old and valedictorian of her high school, Maria Flores Garcia, and her mother are being held in a detention facility in Louisiana, far from their family and community.
In California, an 8-year-old boy, whose identity hasn’t been publicly announced, is being detained by ICE right now. He received a letter instructing him to meet with an ICE agent, and his uncle brought him to the appointment “because he didn’t want to break the law.” The agent took the boy into custody, leaving his uncle distraught and a young boy separated from his family and his school.
[**Use this link to call your representatives to demand the release of Maria Flores Garcia and the 8-year-old boy in California.**](https://act.votolatino.org/call/call-your-representative/?source=em20261114-777&t=1&akid=777%2E1366028%2EXAOYYI)
**Both of these families did everything by the book. They showed up to their routine appointments with the Department of Homeland Security, just as they were asked to. And they were detained anyway.**
This is happening to children across the country. **Since January 2025, 8,755 children have been detained by ICE.** Families are being torn apart without due process, and kids are paying the price.
While we’re proud of the major wins we celebrated in this election, **we can’t take our foot off the gas while our communities are under attack.** Our elected officials need to hear from us, and we need them to take action now.
**[Call your representatives today and demand the release of these two children, and speak out against the incarceration of children in immigration detention centers.](https://act.votolatino.org/call/call-your-representative/?source=em20261114-777&t=2&akid=777%2E1366028%2EXAOYYI)**
**[Call Your Representative ››](https://act.votolatino.org/call/call-your-representative/?source=em20261114-777&t=3&akid=777%2E1366028%2EXAOYYI)**
Thank you,
Voto Latino

The Democrat party is rolling out a new strategy to destroy our democratic republic- Destroying the electoral college.
Following the Democrat's historic blue tsunami in early November, over-confident candidate elects, ranging from state legislators to governors, are pushing for the elimination of the electoral college. The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (NPVIC) has quickly become a key priority for numerous states, functioning as an agreement between states to pledge their electoral votes to the presidential candidate who wins the national popular vote, not the candidate who wins in their state.
The agreement would only come into effect after a coalition of states with a combined 270 electoral votes pass laws joining the agreement. Currently, the compact only has 222 electoral votes, although the recent uptick in Democrat-majority states could quickly push the required legislation.

Although Democrats have threatened to pursue national popular vote policies for decades, it has now garnered enough support to be treated seriously.
Arizona, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Nevada, and Wisconsin are the primary targets of the movement. Each of these swing states recently succumbed to Democrat trifectas, drastically changing their legislative capabilities. In each of these five states, lawmakers have **[previously](https://substack.com/redirect/4cfe0801-fbb2-4cbe-a0a2-51c3807e66f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** attempted to file NPVIC within the past two years. While the incoming Democrat governors in Nevada, Arizona, and Michigan have not publicly stated whether or not they would sign NPVIC legislation, other governors have been more vocal about the issue.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro recently said that he thinks "The national popular vote makes sense... I'll work with lawmakers to figure out what the right mechanism is for moving forward on that." **[Wisconsin Governor-elect David Crowley said](https://substack.com/redirect/fb7d0f83-ca70-4eac-a2fa-4d014ec65a6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** he was "interested" in having conversations with the state legislature about passing NPVIC legislation. Senate leaders in both Michigan and Arizona have expressed interest in pursuing NPVIC legislation.

The national popular vote debate has repeatedly resurfaced during Republican Presidential administrations. While the concept first emerged in liberal circles during the 1960s, it became a serious movement in 2000 after George W. Bush won the Presidency through the Electoral College. The following year, Akhil Reed Amar and Vikram David Amar, two brothers working as constitutional law professors, put together a plan to change how presidents were elected without amending the constitution.
Akhil Reed Amar has recently **[spoken out](https://substack.com/redirect/a186eb44-3d10-4f28-974a-b3a01b96444e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** against the national popular vote despite being one of its architects. He has warned that it could easily be misused during tight races; for instance, states could hypothetically leave a compact during close elections or their local courts could nullify their participation in the compact, leaving election results in limbo. Akhil Reed Amar, despite identifying as a liberal Democrat and claiming to have voted for Hillary Clinton in 2016, considers himself a constitutional originalist. In 2018, he **[testified](https://substack.com/redirect/1400ec46-3f67-4bc4-9d8c-d55b3fc76916?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **on behalf of Supreme Court Trump appointee Brett Kavanaugh, showing that he was willing to cross party lines. His recent hesitations about implementing NPVIC could indicate that the bipartisan vision he originally had has crumbled.
Today, two of the largest groups lobbying for the implementation of NPVIC include FairVote and the League of Women Voters, both of which pursue extremely liberal policy agendas.
**[FairVote](https://substack.com/redirect/378666f5-3110-4fbb-b081-af88ca47a423?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** has worked with radicals like New York state Attorney General Letitia James to pursue rank choice voting and Democrat US Rep. Jamie Raskin has praised FairVote as being "profound." FairVote has also been endorsed by the NAACP, the ACLU, and the National Black Caucus of State Legislators.
The League of Women Voters is perhaps one of the **[largest left-wing lobbying organizations](https://substack.com/redirect/2d54df15-c3e7-4838-82e7-7cb7b1279067?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. They currently oppose voter ID requirements, choice schools, and the death penalty, while advocating for universal healthcare and transgender athletes participating in women's sports.
NPVIC is being used as a weapon by Democrat legislators across the country. It is incrementally working to tear apart both the Electoral College and our country's democratic integrity.

Since election night, there has been a lot of talk about Democrats winning races no one thought they could win.
Texas, the state everyone called solidly red, elected a Democratic governor and sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate. Mississippi, which hasn't elected a Democratic senator since 1982, just did. And it chose someone who was not a Washington insider.
So is Texas a blue state now? Has Mississippi turned blue? Did most people in two states change what they believe in just two years?
I don't believe they did. I don't think the people of Mississippi or Texas woke up one morning and gave up on freedom.
The question we should be asking is a simple one: Did the people leave the Republican Party, or did the Party leave the people?
**The voters didn 't switch. They stayed home.**
The numbers tell the story. Republican voters mostly stayed home, while Democrats turned out unusually well for a midterm. Only a small share of voters actually switched sides.
In Texas, about 11.4 million people voted in 2024. This year, about 9.8 million did, even though the state added more than 400,000 registered voters. Greg Abbott got 30% fewer votes than Trump did two years ago. Gina Hinojosa got 8% more votes than Kamala Harris.
The drop was sharpest where Republicans count on winning big. Roughly 90% of the Texas counties where turnout fell were rural. One analyst estimates about 625,000 Republicans simply sat this one out.
Mississippi followed the same pattern. Across six Southern states including ours, turnout fell 19% in counties Harris won and 26% in counties Trump won. Meanwhile, Black voters went from an estimated 30% of Mississippi's electorate in 2024 to 33% this year.
And the voters who did show up mostly stayed loyal. Exit polls found only 6% of Republicans nationally voted for a Democrat for the House. Republicans didn't abandon their party. They just didn't see a reason to show up for it.
**Who is standing up for Bob?**
[Congressman Chip Roy of Texas ](https://substack.com/redirect/4267c504-f56f-4a88-b94c-809e4b19b611?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)gave a speech on the House floor earlier this week that explains a lot of this. Most of it was about Congress and his home state, but much of what he said is just as true in Mississippi.
Roy read from a post on X about a man named Bob: a 49-year-old blue-collar worker, a three-time Trump voter, whose son did everything right and still can't find work. The post ends with a question that every Republican in Mississippi should have to answer:
> "You've spent a decade demanding Bob's loyalty. You've given him stagnant wages, unaffordable groceries, another foreign war, and a son who did everything right but can't find work. And when they complain, you call them lazy. What possible reason have you given Bob and his son to vote Republican? Do you honestly think you deserve their vote?"
Roy's own verdict was blunt: "I listen to politicians on both sides of the aisle just blithely ignore the plight of the hardworking average American right now wondering what is happening." He said Republicans lost because "they were focused on themselves and the ruling class and not the people."
**" So many proteins to choose from"**
If you want one example of the problem in Mississippi, look at Scott Colom's most effective ad. It has gotten national attention, it didn't make me want to vote for him. But honestly, it made me want to vote against Cindy Hyde-Smith.
The ad used a clip from a February interview on WLOX. A reporter asked what Republicans were doing about the rising price of beef. Hyde-Smith answered, "And you know, you have so many proteins to choose from."
She is a cattle rancher and sits on the Senate Agriculture Committee. Meanwhile, families here are watching the price of ground beef climb every time they go to the store. To a lot of Mississippians, that answer sounded like beef is for people who can afford it, and everyone else can eat something cheaper.
That is what out of touch looks like. And notice I didn't say Republicans. There are plenty of Democrats in that camp too. These folks truly do not care about you or me. They care about power, influence and money, their money.
**Betrayed a little at a time**
Two years ago, ordinary people voted overwhelmingly for Trump and Republicans. These were folks who aren't very political and don't worship either party. Little by little, they were let down.
Congress didn't do its job. The Republican-led Congress never passed the cuts to waste and fraud that DOGE found. As Roy pointed out, it has not passed a single bill to make Trump's border security policies permanent. And it kept spending money that is sinking our country deeper into debt.
The economy didn't get better for regular people. Establishment folks will tell us the economy is doing great. But most people don't measure the economy by the stock market. They measure it by gas so expensive they can't afford a vacation, and by the price of beef going up every time they go to the store. The MAHA reforms people were promised haven't happened either, and the grifters are still getting paid.
Then came the war. For years, conservative commentators warned over and over that a war with Iran could lead to World War III, and that preventing one was reason enough to vote for Trump. Then Trump went to war with Iran, and many of those same voices changed their tune. Now war is good. Even Roy, who said the case for striking Iran might be strong, said the President never came to Congress and never earned the people's support for it.
**Can the Republican Party win them back?**
The people of Mississippi sent a loud message to the political class, both in Jackson and in Washington: we are tired of being ignored. Pay attention to the people who elect you, or we won't vote for you again.
I'd like to believe the Republican Party will hear that message. Honestly, I'm not sure it will. The arrogance, and the sheer dislike some of these leaders have for the common person, has been exposed. It is going to take more than one loss to force real change.
Roy ended his speech with a simple instruction for anyone who wants to lead: "Start with the people." The voters didn't leave. They're still here, still believing what they believed two years ago. The question is whether the Republican Party will come back to them.

Here’s the inside scoop — on what just happened and what comes next
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143458477/660279792/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjZlZjgzYjNjLTRlZTAtZjExMS05MWYwLTAwMGQzYTE4ZTI0NCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=0r2WZRHieDKoN2lM1c9aoSjBEcd8R5rRcxcUN4y1I-8=&emci=04c0a3e0-82df-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&emdi=6ef83b3c-4ee0-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&ceid=8431045)

Peter, **Any definitive recap of the 2026 midterm elections has to center this basic fact: Republicans tried to rig the election by launching a nationwide mid-decade gerrymandering blitzkrieg — but Democrats stopped them. ** The GOP scheme failed because Republicans underestimated the relentless resistance they would face from the American people. And their gerrymandering plot was dismantled — and then destroyed — by the well-organized, multi-pronged strategy executed by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee and its affiliates under the leadership of Attorney General Eric Holder — powered by people like you who raised your voices across the country. _**How It Started**_ Last summer, Donald Trump launched a national gerrymandering crisis. Back then, Republicans boasted that they could pick up 21+ new seats by enacting egregious mid-decade gerrymanders across the country. The Trump administration started utilizing the executive branch to pressure state lawmakers and governors. It was a corrupt and expansive use of federal taxpayer-funded time and resources to advance Republicans’ plot to rig the 2026 midterms. What’s so important to remember is that when they launched this scheme, we were seeing major institutions, including big law firms, folding to Trump again and again. So Republicans assumed Democrats would not — or could not — fight back. They assumed that they could insulate themselves from accountability at the ballot box. They were wrong. _**How We Fought Back**_ Attorney General Holder said it best to Chris Hayes on MS NOW last month, “This effort of theirs didn’t just fall apart. It was destroyed by that which we did.” It was an outstanding, awe-inspiring effort. And because of it, the will of the people prevailed at the ballot box this November. Three key dynamics in the redistricting fight helped to achieve this result:
1. Democrats quickly united behind Attorney General Holder’s proposed response strategy: When Texas moved to enact an egregious mid-decade gerrymander, Attorney General Holder outlined a path forward for Democrats to respond. This led California voters to overwhelmingly back a countermeasure to Texas’ mid-decade gerrymander.
2. Overwhelming public opposition thwarted redraws in several red states: Our affiliate, Redistricting Action, worked in red states across the country to empower citizens to organize, protest, contact their elected leaders, and testify in redistricting hearings against mid-decade gerrymandering. Overwhelming public opposition led Republicans to abandon mid-decade redraws in Nebraska, Kansas, Indiana, New Hampshire, South Carolina, and Georgia.
3. Fair maps advocates took this fight to court — and won: A court victory in Utah paved the way for a fair map with a competitive district for Democrats. Meanwhile, in Missouri, the fair maps movement’s successful legal fight went all the way up to the U.S. Supreme Court — and those victories blocked the Show Me State’s mid-decade gerrymander for this election.

_**Democrats Defeated the Republican Gerrymandering Scheme (for Now)**_ The result of Republicans' gerrymandering scheme coming out of the 2026 midterms was utter and complete failure. In the end, Republicans made no real gains in any of the states where they’d enacted mid-decade gerrymanders. Meanwhile, Democrats are also seeing gains in red states where mid-decade redraws were thwarted over the past year, including South Carolina, Georgia, Indiana, and Kansas. The energy and organization required to beat back these broadly unpopular anti-democracy efforts helped catapult turnout in favor of Democrats in these states. Between enacting egregious gerrymanders against the will of their own constituents and facing a well-organized, well-executed Democratic response, Republicans’ haphazard gerrymandering scheme poked the bear in the eye — and they got mauled at the ballot box. **Now, let's never freaking let that happen again.** _**The Fight Ahead**_ Given these disastrous results for Republicans, we fully expect that they will double down on their gerrymandering schemes after the midterms. Instead of changing course or moderating their policy positions, they will continue down the path of zero-sum politics because they are comfortable ignoring the will of the voters to hold onto power. Republicans in places like Texas and Mississippi could even try to redraw their maps during potential lame-duck sessions this year. The NDRC goal remains the same: fight back in real time against threats to fair maps and ultimately pass a federal ban on partisan gerrymandering and mid-decade redistricting to end this crisis for good. If Republicans continue down this path, we know how to fight them, and based on the election results, we are in an even stronger position to do it. With the ballot measures voters approved and defeated and the state elections Democrats won, blue states now have more power to respond by redrawing their maps, and we will be ready to help them do so. **Bottom line: The fight goes on. But your efforts — combined with the hard work of fair maps champions across the country — have set us up for success, as long as we continue pressing forward for a truly representative democracy.** Thank you for holding firm for fair maps and fair elections. It paid off. The next fights will bring even more twists and turns — so stay tuned. Biz John Bisognano

The minute I received a summons to appear in court on November 16th, I knew I had to write to you. **You see, my fellow journalist Cam Higby and I are facing TWO FELONY CHARGES in retaliation for exposing Minnesota’s weak, vulnerable election system.** If this Soros-funded prosecutor gets her way, we’re both headed to jail. And I need to know today... **[Will you stand by us as we fight these trumped-up charges?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) **
---
[ **STAND WITH JAMES** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
My friend, you know the truth:
---
* These charges are an attempt to criminalize investigative journalism.
* These charges are an attempt to distract from what our reporting exposed as insecure elections in Minnesota.
* These charges are now the basis for a landmark 1st Amendment case where everyone’s right to speak truth to power is on the line.

---
Here’s what REALLY happened in Hennepin County.
---
* >> We never applied for a ballot.
* >> We talked to election clerks, asking questions and getting answers so that Americans could know what was really happening in the elections.
* >> We never signed an affidavit, procured a ballot, or even touched a ballot.

---
Even the Soros-funded prosecutor admitted we never intended to vote. So, where’s the crime? There is no crime. **This is about prosecuting and persecuting citizen journalists. It’s intimidation pure and simple.** Well my friend, I’m not backing down. **[And I need to know right away if you’ll help fight this fight as long as necessary... through whatever trial and appeals are necessary... all the way to the Supreme Court if needs be.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** Because a court battle like this takes resources. So I’m asking you to stand with us today. **[Please make your most generous contribution to the O’Keefe Media Group Foundation today to help fund our legal defense and stand up for the rights of independent journalists.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**

The first three words of the United States Constitution may be the most important in American government: **" We the People."** Those words were intentional. The Constitution does not begin with "We the politicians." It does not say "We the bureaucrats," "We the judges," or even "We the government." It begins with **We the People**. The Constitution's Preamble declares that "We the People of the United States" ordained and established the Constitution. Article I then places the federal government's legislative power in Congress, with members of the House chosen by the people.

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

House Democrats had the chance to advance efforts to impeach incompetent
War Secretary Pete Hegseth this week — but 11 of them missed the vote.

Where were they after voters handed them two huge majorities at the ballot
box?

Four members were down the street surrounded by lobbyists at a fundraising
event hosted by Elect Democratic Women, a major pass-through for AIPAC.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261114.Ex_Ioy&refcode=em20261114-38432&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38432%2E1203867%2E8rsvp6 ]Drop Site: Democrats Missed Hegseth Impeachment Vote While at a
Fundraiser with Defense Lobbyists. The new member reception was hosted by
Elect Democratic Women, a major pass-through for AIPAC this cycle, and was
attended by more than 100 lobbyists.

According to Drop Site, the reception included more than 100 lobbyists
representing defense contractors, weapons makers, AI companies, crypto
firms, insurance companies, and Big Pharma. Reps. Julia Brownley, Melanie
Stansbury, Brittany Pettersen, and Laura Gillen were there instead of
voting on the House floor.

You may remember AIPAC’s super PAC, United Democracy Project, used this
vaguely named group to funnel millions of dollars into 2026 Democratic
primaries while hiding its identity from voters.

EDW then gave $2.4 million to another shadow PAC, which spent $1.5 million
against Justice Democrat Melat Kiros in CO-01. They also tried (and
failed) to buy the IL-09 seat where JD candidate Kat Abughazaleh ran, but
successfully won the IL-08 primary against JD candidate Junaid Ahmed.

It’s unacceptable that these Democrats failed to meet the moment and do
their jobs to impeach Hegseth, especially knowing they chose to hang out
with Lockheed Martin reps and other lobbyists at an AIPAC-backed
fundraiser instead.

It’s a prime reminder that AIPAC and its right-wing billionaire-funded
network still hold an immense amount of power in Washington, and they’re
getting better at hiding it.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261114.Ex_Ioy&refcode=em20261114-38432&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1003&akid=38432%2E1203867%2E8rsvp6 ]Justice Democrats don’t take a penny from AIPAC, its network, or any
corporate super PACS — and our growing bloc is ready to keep fighting
their influence in the halls of Congress. If you’re with us, pitch in a
grassroots contribution today.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261114.Ex_Ioy&refcode=em20261114-38432&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1022&akid=38432%2E1203867%2E8rsvp6 ]Contribute $5

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

Contribute to Justice Democrats: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20261114-38432-footer&t=1023&refcode2=38432_1203867_8rsvp6&akid=38432%2E1203867%2E8rsvp6

#
# **HAPPENING THIS MORNING!**
[_**Philly Reads Literacy Summit**_](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172733.172729.462&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18974) _**Join us this morning for free breakfast and reading workshops for students, educators, and parents**_ **Come to the School of the Future and reserve your spot on-site! **
* * *
We're offering a half day of panel discussions, workshops, and children's health services so our entire community can come together to discuss the issues we're seeing, learn about solutions, and walk away with peace of mind that we will improve reading proficiency across the city.

body:
# [#]
Friends and Supporters,

I’m proud of my service. While these results are neither what my team and I worked for nor hoped for, I’m grateful to the hundreds of local elected officials and community leaders who supported our campaign and every volunteer who put up a sign, collected petition signatures, made phone calls, knocked on doors, and talked to their neighbors. And I’m especially grateful to my wife, Jan, our family, and my incredible staff.

My team and I have always lived by one principle: We’re here to do the people’s work serving our district, and that job is never too big nor too small. None of our success would have been possible without the partnership of our outstanding community.

When Washington diverted water killing 80,000 spawning salmon in the Klamath River, we captured national headlines by dropping 500 pounds of dead salmon on the steps of the U.S. Department of the Interior. Our protest led to the waterflow restoration and salmon are again spawning in the Klamath.

As our country grappled with the growing impacts of climate change, I worked with local and national leaders to write and enact the largest investment in combating climate change in U.S. history. My landmark renewable energy policies helped drive down energy costs, generated $400 billion in U.S. investments, and created 400,000 jobs.

At the height of our gun violence epidemic, I was tasked with chairing the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, where I helped write and pass the most significant gun violence prevention reform signed into law in decades. To this day, our law is helping to keep guns out of the hands of domestic abusers and targeting illegal gun trafficking.

And when our community was devastated by raging wildfires, we came together. I secured $99 million for recovery and I passed legislation through one of the most divided Congresses in decades to deliver $500 million in tax relief for survivors.

We also passed my bill preserving over 273,000 acres in Northern California as wilderness and allowing the use of mechanized equipment to prevent and fight fires in wilderness areas.

My work to protect our natural lands didn’t end there. I led the effort to designate and expand Berryessa Snow Mountain National Monument and through my position on the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission, I protected over 4.75 million acres of wetlands and uplands for the next generation to enjoy.

When proposed water diversions threatened our community, I fought hard to stop diversions that would have devastated North of Delta agriculture and harmed fish and migratory birds.

When our ag community faced threats, I passed a law for rice farmers that kept them afloat, authored the historic tax credits for rice farmers to flood their lands and protect both their crops and endangered species, secured critical funding to fight pests like the glassy-winged sharpshooter, delivered funds to study and combat the impact of wildfire smoke exposure on winegrapes, created a pilot USDA insurance program offered to California winegrape farmers, and delivered millions to save peach farmers on the brink of disaster.

And when a pandemic spread around the world, my bill was passed providing telehealth access to patients, ensuring Americans could safely access the care they needed.

It’s been the honor of my life to serve the community where I was born, grew up, and still live today. I look forward to continuing to serve our community through the end of my term and beyond.

Thank you for all of your support.

Mike Thompson

Anyone who’s spent time on the water in Hampton Roads knows that the tide always turns.
Four years ago, I lost this seat. I didn’t second-guess the fight then, and I’m glad I didn’t.
On November 3rd, the tide turned.
The people of Hampton Roads sent me back to Congress. And we weren’t alone. Across the country, voters delivered a blue wave that flipped the House with what’s on track to be the largest Democratic majority in decades. Democrats flipped Senate seats in places like Kansas, Texas, and Ohio to take back that chamber too.
All cycle, I said Democrats needed to flip just three House seats to take back the majority. We blew right past that number, and VA-02 was one of the seats that got us there.
I’m proud of that. I’m also not one to oversell, so here’s the plain truth about how we did it:
We spent down to zero.
When you’re in a Toss-Up race against an incumbent and a flood of outside money, you don’t hold anything in reserve. You leave it all on the deck.
Every dollar went into this victory. That was the right call. But it means that before I’m sworn in, we need to settle up.

| | Peter, Stop for a second and take in what you’ve been part of these past eleven days: **Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan** — the first Native American woman elected to the U.S. Senate in the 237 years it has existed. **Governor-elect Deb Haaland** — the first Native American woman elected governor of any state, in a state that barred her people from voting until 1948. **Congresswoman Sharice Davids** — re-elected, defending the ground where this movement first broke through in 2018. **Congresswoman-elect Claire Valdez** — elected with 83%, proof the movement is still growing. **And Mary Peltola — now at 49.8% in the last uncalled Senate race in America,** her lead grown to roughly ten thousand votes, two-tenths of a point from a majority, with Tuesday’s tabulation expected to finish what every count since Election Day has pointed toward: the fifth win, the completed sweep, and one more Democratic seat in the Senate. None of this was supposed to be possible. Every forecaster, every super PAC, every courtroom maneuver said so. It happened anyway — because candidates this good met a movement this stubborn, funded about twenty-four dollars at a time by people like you. So today’s ask looks different than usual. Yes, the watch continues through Tuesday’s tabulation and the November 25 certification — the investigations and noise haven’t stopped, and neither have we. But this is also about what comes after: Indigenous Women Lead PAC exists so that what happened this November never has to be a miracle again. Recruiting the next Mary. Training the next Peggy. Funding the next Claire from her first primary. The next generation of Indigenous women who run — in 2028, in statehouses, in places nobody thinks winnable yet — starts with what this movement does right now. **One : The census is the lever**
In 2000, 31.1 million Americans were foreign-born -- about one in nine. In January 2025 the foreign-born population hit 53.3 million, 15.8 percent of the country: the highest count and share ever recorded, above the 1890 peak. Then enforcement changed the slope, not the mountain. Pew counted 51.9 million by June; the Center for Immigration Studies counted 2.2 million fewer by July; the Census Bureau reports net international migration down in every state and most counties; CBO slashed its 2025 net-immigration estimate from two million to 410,000.
But the surge is banked. The people who arrived between 2021 and 2024 are in the denominators now, and citizenship is a lagging indicator -- naturalizations have been running past 800,000 a year, so a large share of the surge can convert to voters before the 2030 census.
Which is the lever. The Fourteenth Amendment says "persons in each State," not _citizens_ ; that has been the law of apportionment since 1868. On September 9, 2026, the administration proposed to break it -- a 2030 census counting only citizens and green-card holders, excluding the undocumented, asylum seekers, and anyone without permanent status. The New York Times mapped the seats that would migrate out of the immigrant-heavy coasts toward the interior. The rule isn't settled. It gets settled by whoever holds the presidency in 2028 and 2029, because the census design is signed in the two years after the inaugural. Persons counted: the demographic drift of the last quarter century flows through to Congress for two more decades. Persons excluded: a bloc of House seats -- and every electoral vote attached to them -- moves inland.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/018c8a1c-dd47-47b8-894b-a7a48866120f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The counter-program is public: statehood for D.C. (one House seat, two senators) and Puerto Rico (four or five House seats, two senators). The House passed D.C. statehood 232-180 in 2021; Puerto Ricans voted 58 percent for statehood in 2024; the DSA-aligned wing is among the loudest sponsors. Four new senators no serious model expects to elect a Republican this decade, five or six House votes, and a filibuster-proof appetite for everything else on the list. That is not a Congress nudged at the margins. It is a Congress re-weighted at the floor.
**Two : The tax that needs no vote...**

That is not a Congress nudged at the margins. It is a Congress re-weighted at the floor.
**Two : The tax that needs no vote**
In 2000 the national debt was $5.7 trillion, 55 percent of GDP. It is roughly $38 trillion now, with debt held by the public at 100 percent of GDP. CBO's February 2026 outlook: a $1.9 trillion deficit this fiscal year; net interest crossing $1 trillion this year; debt at 120 percent of GDP by 2036; interest exceeding defense spending every year of the outlook and nearly doubling it by 2036, consuming from 19 to 26 percent of federal revenue. Stretch the window and CBO's long-term outlook has debt at 156 percent of GDP by 2055 -- revised toward 172 percent under current law. These are not activist numbers. They are the accountant's numbers. Read it again.
Now the inflation half of the ledger. Between January 2020 and January 2025 the price level rose about 23 percent -- the fastest reset since the early 1980s. The proximate cause was a pandemic fiscal wave, debt-financed and then papered over; the debt is that inflation's principal, the price index its interest. And the projection needs no model: a state spending a quarter of its revenue on interest does not abolish programs. It inflates them slowly. Tolerated negative real rates, benefits indexed stingily, the dollar shaved a point a year until the debt is yesterday's news and groceries are next week's problem. Inflation is the only tax that never appears on a ballot, and by 2050 it will have quietly financed everything anyone promises between now and then.
**Three : The hospital is the economy**
Since 2000 the economy added roughly 28 million jobs, and about four in ten of them are in health care or social assistance. Manufacturing shed four and a half million net. _The hospital replaced the factory_ , and the replacement accelerates: BLS's September 2026 projections give the whole economy 5.9 million new jobs by 2035, with healthcare support the fastest-growing occupational group at 13.3 percent, healthcare practitioners second, and the two healthcare groups together supplying about a third of every new job created. The single largest occupation being added in America is _**home health** and **personal care aide**_.
Follow it to 2050. The 65-and-over population goes from 58 million (17 percent) to about 82 million (23 percent) -- one American in four past retirement. Health care is already one dollar in five of GDP, rising on every CMS trend line. The labor market's shape is an hourglass: AI-adjacent technical work concentrated at the top in a few metros; millions of care jobs at the bottom paid at the edge of poverty; the middle -- where the 2000s internet boom built its career ladders -- hollowing out. And the bottom rung is an immigration story too: home health aides are among the most immigrant-heavy workforces in the country. The jobs ledger and the census ledger are the same ledger. The same people are recruited to fill the beds, then counted -- or not counted -- to draw the districts.
**Four : The classroom that can't check the paperwork**
The pipeline that staffs the middle of that hourglass is failing its own audits. In 2022 NAEP recorded the largest drop in nine-year-old reading in the test's thirty-year history. By 2024, twelfth-grade reading was the lowest _ever_ measured and twelfth-grade math the lowest in two decades, while chronic absenteeism -- 15 percent before the pandemic -- roughly doubled and stayed doubled. College enrollment never recovered its 2010 peak; it is down about three million students, hundreds of campuses have closed or merged, and Gallup's confidence in higher education fell from 57 percent in 2015 to the mid-30s.
Project that forward and 2050 contains two school systems in one country: a slim elite track tuned for AI-adjacent work, and a mass track running through certificates into the care economy, with reading levels that make a census form, a loan disclosure, or a ballot initiative the hardest document a graduate reads that year. A republic that cannot staff its auditors, clerks and technicians does not get to complain about who runs its institutions. It outsources them.
**Five : The platform, not the plot**
None of this requires a conspiracy, because none of it is a secret. The census rule change is a published proposal. Statehood is filed legislation that already passed one chamber. The **Judiciary Act of 2021** would add four justices, and the campaign trail now floats thirteen or fifteen. The assault-weapons ban passed the House 217-213 in 2022 and awaits a bench that re-reads "common use." The speech regime arrives as safety -- campus codes, platform-compliance templates imported from the EU's Digital Services Act, "harm" categories widening one definition at a time. Each item polls individually reasonable. The sum is a licensing society nobody voted on, anchored by a Senate re-weighted by four votes and a Court of fifteen who serve for life.
And the presidency? "Moot" is the precise word. Once the Senate is re-weighted and the Court is fifteen, the White House alternates without reversing. Personnel change; direction does not. The office that makes the headlines stops making the decisions -- _the most durable form of presidential irrelevance ever devised_.
A plot needs conspirators. A platform just needs a majority and a calendar. Everything above is the second thing.
**Who decided?**
The Fourteenth Amendment did, when it counted persons. The Congresses since 2001 did, when they borrowed. The retirement curve did, when it booked the beds. The 2050 question is not who decided -- the answer will be sitting in the apportionment file. The question is whether anyone still reading the file was taught to read it.
