The Arithmetic of the Post-Trump Quarter-Century | | | Nov 14 | | | | | | | | | | | | One : The census is the lever In 2000, 31.1 million Americans were foreign-born -- about one in nine. In January 2025 the foreign-born population hit 53.3 million, 15.8 percent of the country: the highest count and share ever recorded, above the 1890 peak. Then enforcement changed the slope, not the mountain. Pew counted 51.9 million by June; the Center for Immigration Studies counted 2.2 million fewer by July; the Census Bureau reports net international migration down in every state and most counties; CBO slashed its 2025 net-immigration estimate from two million to 410,000. But the surge is banked. The people who arrived between 2021 and 2024 are in the denominators now, and citizenship is a lagging indicator -- naturalizations have been running past 800,000 a year, so a large share of the surge can convert to voters before the 2030 census. Which is the lever. The Fourteenth Amendment says "persons in each State," not citizens ; that has been the law of apportionment since 1868. On September 9, 2026, the administration proposed to break it -- a 2030 census counting only citizens and green-card holders, excluding the undocumented, asylum seekers, and anyone without permanent status. The New York Times mapped the seats that would migrate out of the immigrant-heavy coasts toward the interior. The rule isn't settled. It gets settled by whoever holds the presidency in 2028 and 2029, because the census design is signed in the two years after the inaugural. Persons counted: the demographic drift of the last quarter century flows through to Congress for two more decades. Persons excluded: a bloc of House seats -- and every electoral vote attached to them -- moves inland. | | ---|---|--- The counter-program is public: statehood for D.C. (one House seat, two senators) and Puerto Rico (four or five House seats, two senators). The House passed D.C. statehood 232-180 in 2021; Puerto Ricans voted 58 percent for statehood in 2024; the DSA-aligned wing is among the loudest sponsors. Four new senators no serious model expects to elect a Republican this decade, five or six House votes, and a filibuster-proof appetite for everything else on the list. That is not a Congress nudged at the margins. It is a Congress re-weighted at the floor. Two : The tax that needs no vote In 2000 the national debt was $5.7 trillion, 55 percent of GDP. It is roughly $38 trillion now, with debt held by the public at 100 percent of GDP. CBO's February 2026 outlook: a $1.9 trillion deficit this fiscal year; net interest crossing $1 trillion this year; debt at 120 percent of GDP by 2036; interest exceeding defense spending every year of the outlook and nearly doubling it by 2036, consuming from 19 to 26 percent of federal revenue. Stretch the window and CBO's long-term outlook has debt at 156 percent of GDP by 2055 -- revised toward 172 percent under current law. These are not activist numbers. They are the accountant's numbers. Read it again. Now the inflation half of the ledger. Between January 2020 and January 2025 the price level rose about 23 percent -- the fastest reset since the early 1980s. The proximate cause was a pandemic fiscal wave, debt-financed and then papered over; the debt is that inflation's principal, the price index its interest. And the projection needs no model: a state spending a quarter of its revenue on interest does not abolish programs. It inflates them slowly. Tolerated negative real rates, benefits indexed stingily, the dollar shaved a point a year until the debt is yesterday's news and groceries are next week's problem. Inflation is the only tax that never appears on a ballot, and by 2050 it will have quietly financed everything anyone promises between now and then. Three : The hospital is the economy Since 2000 the economy added roughly 28 million jobs, and about four in ten of them are in health care or social assistance. Manufacturing shed four and a half million net. The hospital replaced the factory , and the replacement accelerates: BLS's September 2026 projections give the whole economy 5.9 million new jobs by 2035, with healthcare support the fastest-growing occupational group at 13.3 percent, healthcare practitioners second, and the two healthcare groups together supplying about a third of every new job created. The single largest occupation being added in America is home health and personal care aide. Follow it to 2050. The 65-and-over population goes from 58 million (17 percent) to about 82 million (23 percent) -- one American in four past retirement. Health care is already one dollar in five of GDP, rising on every CMS trend line. The labor market's shape is an hourglass: AI-adjacent technical work concentrated at the top in a few metros; millions of care jobs at the bottom paid at the edge of poverty; the middle -- where the 2000s internet boom built its career ladders -- hollowing out. And the bottom rung is an immigration story too: home health aides are among the most immigrant-heavy workforces in the country. The jobs ledger and the census ledger are the same ledger. The same people are recruited to fill the beds, then counted -- or not counted -- to draw the districts. Four : The classroom that can't check the paperwork The pipeline that staffs the middle of that hourglass is failing its own audits. In 2022 NAEP recorded the largest drop in nine-year-old reading in the test's thirty-year history. By 2024, twelfth-grade reading was the lowest ever measured and twelfth-grade math the lowest in two decades, while chronic absenteeism -- 15 percent before the pandemic -- roughly doubled and stayed doubled. College enrollment never recovered its 2010 peak; it is down about three million students, hundreds of campuses have closed or merged, and Gallup's confidence in higher education fell from 57 percent in 2015 to the mid-30s. Project that forward and 2050 contains two school systems in one country: a slim elite track tuned for AI-adjacent work, and a mass track running through certificates into the care economy, with reading levels that make a census form, a loan disclosure, or a ballot initiative the hardest document a graduate reads that year. A republic that cannot staff its auditors, clerks and technicians does not get to complain about who runs its institutions. It outsources them. Five : The platform, not the plot None of this requires a conspiracy, because none of it is a secret. The census rule change is a published proposal. Statehood is filed legislation that already passed one chamber. The Judiciary Act of 2021 would add four justices, and the campaign trail now floats thirteen or fifteen. body:
See the story that shaped me.
|
---
| | | | [](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
---
| | |
---
| | Friend,
My name is Katie Britt, and if it’s alright with you, I’d like to share a little about who I am. **I’m not part of the D.C. cocktail circuit, and I never will be._That’s just not who I am._**

In 2022, I was elected to represent the great state of Alabama in the United States Senate. I became the first woman in Alabama’s history to hold this seat—but that’s not why I ran.

I ran because I’m a _**mom**_ , a _**wife**_ , and a _**conservative**_ who’s fed up with the direction this country is heading. I came to Washington to fight for our families, to protect our values, and to bring some Alabama backbone to a broken system.

I didn’t come here to make friends with the political elite. I came here to stand up for the people who don’t have a voice in the room—and I’m not backing down.
---
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
Before coming to the Senate, I served as the first female president and CEO of the Business Council of Alabama, and before that, I was Chief of Staff to Senator Richard Shelby. **I’ve never shied away from a challenge—and I’ve never forgotten who I’m fighting for.** In every role I’ve held, my mission has been the same: _deliver real results for Alabama families and the American people._
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
Before starting my career in public service, I earned my undergraduate and law degrees from the University of Alabama. That experience taught me how to lead, think on my feet, and fight for what I believe in—**and it laid the foundation for _everything_ I’ve done since.**
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
But long before that, I was just a small-town girl from Enterprise, Alabama. My dad ran the local hardware store. My mom taught dance to almost every kid in town. We didn’t grow up with wealth or political connections. **We came from hard work, grit, and doing things the right way._That’s how I was raised, and that’s exactly how I lead._**
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
My husband Wesley and our two amazing kids are my rock. In 2011, a tornado tore through our home and nearly took our lives. That moment changed everything, and reminded me what truly matters. __**Faith** , **family** , and **resilience**.__
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
I’ve lived a life full of hard work, determination, and breaking barriers. There have been challenges and triumphs alike, but I wouldn’t trade any of it.

My story is a testament to what America stands for—the American Dream. From a small town in Alabama, I rose to become my state’s U.S. Senator—a woman who’s breaking barriers and fighting for conservative values every day.

_**_I’m living proof of the limitless opportunity and freedom that define this country._**_

But, I didn’t get here by playing it safe or staying quiet, **and I’m not about to start now.**

The radical Left wants to _silence_ conservatives like me. They want to drown out our voices and push their agenda without opposition, but I’m standing firm.

I’m fighting tooth and nail to keep up and push back hard, for Alabama, for our values, and for every American who believes in freedom.

**The support I’ve received so far means everything, but this fight is far from over.** We need the resources to keep going strong and hold our ground.

**[So, after hearing a bit of my story, will you take a moment to chip in whatever you can afford to help me keep up this fight? The road ahead won’t be easy, but I’ve faced tough battles before. And it would mean the world to have you standing with me.](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)**
|
---
[CHIP IN TO FIGHT WITH KATIE BRITT >>](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
Thank you, and may God bless America.

Katie Britt (R-AL)
|
---
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---

Do Idaho Republicans still believe that we don't "co-parent with the government"?
# [An Idaho Senator Wants to Hand You the Keys (But They're Already in Your Pocket)](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=10730337&post_id=224919468&utm_source=cross-post&utm_campaign=2114823&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjI0OTE5NDY4LCJpYXQiOjE3OTQ2ODA5NjYsImV4cCI6MTc5NzI3Mjk2NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwNzMwMzM3Iiwic3ViIjoicG9zdC1yZWFjdGlvbiJ9.1K4F9FTFAcVe0SptVcdLU3QxS1zghkb6GnZfAOdhYLo)

| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/righttoparent/p/an-idaho-senator-wants-to-hand-you?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store-no-desktop&inbox=true&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Senator Kevin Cook and I serve together in the Idaho Senate.
Last month he wrote a column in the Post Register called "[App stores must be required to respect parental consent](https://substack.com/redirect/0ab7c01a-f687-4135-91af-2e4a8aa69f6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)."
If you didn't read it, here's the short version of his argument: Phones are a portal to porn and predators, tech companies have "rigged the system to lock parents out," and so he's working on a bill he calls the App Store Protection Act. It would make the app store get a parent's permission before a kid downloads any app. He says the goal is to "put the keys back in the hands of Idaho parents."
Kevin means well, and the danger is real. Everyone knows these platforms hurt kids.
_But his bill doesn 't touch any of that._
Walk through his column with me and you'll see it. He says that when our kids hold a smartphone, "they hold a portal to the entire world."
And there's the crux of the matter, right?
_**Why do your kids hold an unlocked smartphone? Who bought it for them? Who pays for the Wi-Fi? Who gives them unsupervised access to the full internet at night? Why do kids need a smartphone in the first place?**_
They don't.
The whole argument kind of stops here, I think.
Why would you hand your kid something that can harm them and let them run off with it in their room, or drive off with it with their friends? It's like handing them a loaded gun and being surprised when someone gets shot.
Kevin says "giant tech corporations operate like digital gatekeepers," and that parents "must have the final say over what enters their children's hands."
But parents already have the final say on what enters their child's hands, right?
Do children buy a $1,000 iPhone?
Do children pay for Wi-Fi and the internet? No. Mom and Dad do.
The gatekeepers are Mom and Dad, not a tech company. Saying parents are left out of what goes on the phone is like saying they're left out of who drives the family car. You already make decisions about your family and your kids every day: what's for dinner, who drives them where, bedtime, screen time, etc.
You don't need permission to make those decisions.
And you don't need it here either.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2c9cb9a5-fc7f-4471-acbc-5df6dd801aa2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Then he says tech companies _" rigged the system to lock parents out."_
This is just fundamentally untrue. Have you ever set up parental controls on an iPhone? I have. It takes like 5 minutes and it's free. Right now, today, you can make your kid ask permission before downloading any app. That's the exact thing Kevin's bill promises, it already exists, and nobody has to show an ID or pass a new law to use it.
Parents are absolutely already in the driver's seat.
The problem is lazy parents. The problem is parents who don't want to tell them no. Parents aren't locked out. Many of them caught up in the same game, zonked out on their phones instead of raising their children (go to a restaraunt and observe).
Kevin says we need "a simple principle of accountability."
Agreed. Parents should be accountable for the things they give their children. But then he reaches for beer? He says "We don't blame the farmer who grows barley if a local bar hands beer to a minor," he writes. But "we do expect the clerk at the store to check an ID."
This is completely backwards and actually proves too much. In his own sentence, the bar is the one handing beer to a minor. Fine. So why does his bill card kids in the parking lot? If Facebook's the bar, then his bill never walks inside where underage kids are doing shots. Or, picture a bartender who pours drinks all night and says carding people is "the liquor store's job."
That's his bill.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6f9cb349-d84d-48cd-8e73-dd0b4b527a27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The clerk analogy doesn't help either.
Because the gas station only cards for things that are dangerous to kids (cigarettes, nicotine pouches, beer) and it sells you donuts, energy drinks, and the newspaper without a word.
_**But Kevin 's bill makes everyone upload their government ID before downloading anything at all, from the weather app to the calculator or Bible app.**_
He calls app stores "the electronic storefronts on our phones" that "make financial transactions with children without asking the parent for permission."
Except most apps are free, right?
Kids getting harmed on Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat _aren 't buying anything_, so these aren't storefronts. And if kids are buying things on a phone without their parents' permission, the solution is... parents (not big government).
Again, these are not digital storefronts. Because the harm happens at midnight, when a 14-year-old is still in bed scrolling Instagram. But Kevin's bill is the ticket-taker at a movie theater who checks ages at the door and never checks which theater the kid went into.
If we're going to hold someone accountable, why don't we hold someone accountable who's actually doing the harm? Adult content comes from websites and apps. It doesn't originate in the device or App Store. A smoke detector only helps if it's in the room where the fire is. So, in this case, the fire is inside Instagram.
But Kevin's bill mounts the smoke detector out on the mailbox (the app store) instead.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e47f36ea-2fad-4c38-ade5-881a04fdc00e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Then come his bullet points, which promise that parents "give the green light" on every download and get "real legal teeth" if a company ignores them.
All this does is lock the front door while the garage door, side door, back window and sliding glass door are wide open.
What about the laptop?
What about the browser: Safari, Chrome, DuckDuckGo, stuff like that?
What about a friend's phone or the computer at the library?
All this does is regulate who can download an app. It doesn't regulate what happens when they do, which is where the real harm happens. If a parent says no to Instagram, the kid can still type [instagram.com](https://substack.com/redirect/dd51045b-0b8f-4568-85d9-4a36b4107980?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) into a browser and access the same harm. So again, what are we doing here?
Think about what this looks like in real life.
Under this bill your kid needs your approval for every app, from Instagram to the Bible app to the calculator. It's like signing for every Amazon package that shows up at your door. By Friday you're signing without looking (and signing never told you what was in the box anyway). Tapping "approve" doesn't show you what's inside the app.
As for the legal teeth, Section 8 of the federal version (H.R. 3149) says an app that relied "in good faith" on the age the app store gave it is "deemed not liable." Translation: when a kid gets hurt, the app points at the app store, and the app store points at Mom, who tapped "approve."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a2906b38-d94e-430b-95b8-d62f33fbe7e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So besides creating a liability shield for the social media companies doing the harm, all this really accomplishes is the creation of a digital ID checkpoint for every single human being in Idaho (to know who's a kid, a company has to check who's an adult, which means checking everybody).
Texas started enforcing its version on June 4, 2026. Now every Texan who opens a new account on the app store has to hand over a credit card or a scan of a government ID (don't even get me started on data collection here). A federal judge compared it to carding every customer at a bookstore door, but an appeals court let the law take effect anyway.
Kevin says his bill is about "ensuring parents, not multi-billion-dollar corporations, decide what is appropriate for their own children."
_But parents already do this._
_The good ones, at least._
_No new law or bill needed._
There's a reason we call this "the Grindr bill" (yes, THAT Grindr, the gay hookup app).
Grindr loves this bill and endorsed the federal version. Meta, Snap and X put out a joint statement cheering Utah's version. And Pornhub's parent company is on board with this bill too.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3088ec50-10d4-423d-bc99-a59d58869e50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_**I don 't know what you think, but if there's a "child safety" bill supported by Meta, Pornhub, and Grindr, I'm running in the other direction.**_
Kevin closes by saying tech companies shouldn't get to make contracts with our children "behind our backs."
Behind our backs is the the problem, right?
_What happened to parents... being parents?_
I thought Idaho Republicans used to say, "We don't co-parent with the government."
I still believe that.

Many of them caught up in the same game, zonked out on their phones instead of raising their children (go to a restaraunt and observe). Kevin says we need "a simple principle of accountability." Agreed. Parents should be accountable for the things they give their children. But then he reaches for beer? He says "We don't blame the farmer who grows barley if a local bar hands beer to a minor," he writes. But "we do expect the clerk at the store to check an ID." This is completely backwards and actually proves too much. In his own sentence, the bar is the one handing beer to a minor. Fine. So why does his bill card kids in the parking lot? If Facebook's the bar, then his bill never walks inside where underage kids are doing shots. Or, picture a bartender who pours drinks all night and says carding people is "the liquor store's job." That's his bill. | | ---|---|--- The clerk analogy doesn't help either. Because the gas station only cards for things that are dangerous to kids (cigarettes, nicotine pouches, beer) and it sells you donuts, energy drinks, and the newspaper without a word. But Kevin 's bill makes everyone upload their government ID before downloading anything at all, from the weather app to the calculator or Bible app. He calls app stores "the electronic storefronts on our phones" that "make financial transactions with children without asking the parent for permission." Except most apps are free, right? Kids getting harmed on Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat aren 't buying anything, so these aren't storefronts. And if kids are buying things on a phone without their parents' permission, the solution is... parents (not big government). Again, these are not digital storefronts. Because the harm happens at midnight, when a 14-year-old is still in bed scrolling Instagram. But Kevin's bill is the ticket-taker at a movie theater who checks ages at the door and never checks which theater the kid went into. If we're going to hold someone accountable, why don't we hold someone accountable who's actually doing the harm? Adult content comes from websites and apps. It doesn't originate in the device or App Store. A smoke detector only helps if it's in the room where the fire is. So, in this case, the fire is inside Instagram. But Kevin's bill mounts the smoke detector out on the mailbox (the app store) instead. Then come his bullet points, which promise that parents "give the green light" on every download and get "real legal teeth" if a company ignores them. All this does is lock the front door while the garage door, side door, back window and sliding glass door are wide open. What about the laptop? What about the browser: Safari, Chrome, DuckDuckGo, stuff like that? What about a friend's phone or the computer at the library? All this does is regulate who can download an app. It doesn't regulate what happens when they do, which is where the real harm happens. If a parent says no to Instagram, the kid can still type into a browser and access the same harm. So again, what are we doing here? Think about what this looks like in real life. Under this bill your kid needs your approval for every app, from Instagram to the Bible app to the calculator. It's like signing for every Amazon package that shows up at your door. By Friday you're signing without looking (and signing never told you what was in the box anyway). Tapping "approve" doesn't show you what's inside the app. As for the legal teeth, Section 8 of the federal version (H.R. 3149) says an app that relied "in good faith" on the age the app store gave it is "deemed not liable." Translation: when a kid gets hurt, the app points at the app store, and the app store points at Mom, who tapped "approve." | | ---|---|--- So besides creating a liability shield for the social media companies doing the harm, all this really accomplishes is the creation of a digital ID checkpoint for every single human being in Idaho (to know who's a kid, a company has to check who's an adult, which means checking everybody). Texas started enforcing its version on June 4, 2026. Now every Texan who opens a new account on the app store has to hand over a credit card or a scan of a government ID (don't even get me started on data collection here). A federal judge compared it to carding every customer at a bookstore door, but an appeals court let the law take effect anyway. Kevin says his bill is about "ensuring parents, not multi-billion-dollar corporations, decide what is appropriate for their own children." But parents already do this. The good ones, at least. No new law or bill needed. There's a reason we call this "the Grindr bill" (yes, THAT Grindr, the gay hookup app). Grindr loves this bill and endorsed the federal version. Meta, Snap and X put out a joint statement cheering Utah's version. And Pornhub's parent company is on board with this bill too. | | ---|---|--- I don 't know what you think, but if there's a "child safety" bill supported by Meta, Pornhub, and Grindr, I'm running in the other direction.** Kevin closes by saying tech companies shouldn't get to make contracts with our children "behind our backs." Behind our backs is the the problem, right? What happened to parents... being parents? I thought Idaho Republicans used to say, "We don't co-parent with the government." I still believe that. | | | | | | | | Originally posted on | | | | Lenney ---|---|--- | ? You already have what it takes to protect your kids. You don't need a new law to prove it. (C) 2026 Brian Lenney ? ?

name: Kristan Hawkins
subject: Where is the moral outcry?
body:
A governor just told pro-life states their laws don't count.

*|MC_PREVIEW_TEXT|* | | |
---
| | [](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckMuKhDAQRb8m7lryMuoii4HGXc92lpJOSi0wD5JoM38_OI8fmF3Bgbrn3o_H_DC4Y1jfjQdtT5xzmV8bZMBSN_Axmz0e1ebPmVOubozdmJyNrXjCLE3jtHVK8AY060epBjYK2Wy6F4Z2z34Y6Ai0o4uRdgDrpBucG58KGtTXO8aYZIPsBGvlMlLaLWMH0nWyH4mkR3KmQmltDAXyaa5MDCFeVwytjb7Z9VZrKkS8ET4RPhWwR4a21MNBqGWJeccF2phXwqdkbj9ViJhKtkTcwadMuPJlRUfEnStGeZ8M4eqofrbGJ4NruMiv7B-JoUKoRNztiU3WLr1w37Gonki6eoP7t139x6Cn5l8BAAD__zROhSY)
Dear Pro-Life Friend,

A New York abortionist named Margaret Carpenter mailed chemical abortion pills to a teenage girl in Louisiana.

Abortion is illegal in Louisiana, so Louisiana indicted her.

Then, Louisiana asked New York to send her back to face the charges.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul refused. Her exact words were:
_“I will not be signing an extradition order that came from the governor of Louisiana.**Not now, not ever.** ”_
The people of Louisiana passed laws to protect preborn babies and their mothers, and a governor in New York told them those laws don’t count.

**That’s what abortionist “shield laws” do.** They protect abortionists who ship chemical abortion pills into states where abortion is illegal, and they block those states from holding anyone accountable. New York even lets the abortionist keep their name off the prescription label!

Twenty-two states and Washington, D.C., have now passed shield laws like this.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m President of Students for Life of America. I’ve spent 20 years fighting for preborn babies and their mothers, and I’ve never seen pro-abortion politicians this brazen.

The good news is, pro-life states are fighting back.

Louisiana, Alabama, and Arkansas went straight to the U.S. Supreme Court and sued New York, California, and Massachusetts to strike these shield laws down.

**I believe this will be the next great abortion case in America.**

For years, we’ve been told abortion is now “a state issue.”

_If the pro-abortion states win this case, that phrase means nothing. A handful of blue states will set abortion policy for the entire nation,_one mailbox at a time__.

Before he passed away, the late Justice Antonin Scalia asked a question I’ve carried with me for most of my adult life:

_“I am against abortion. I want to end it! But where is the moral outcry?”_

I intend for Students for Life to be a key part of the solution, but I need you with me today.

[Will you make a generous tax-deductible gift right away to help us stand with the pro-life states in this fight](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckMuKhDAQRb8m7lryMuoii4HGXc92lpJOSi0wD5JoM38_OI8fmF3Bgbrn3o_H_DC4Y1jfjQdtT5xzmV8bZMBSN_Axmz0e1ebPmVOubozdmJyNrXjCLE3jtHVK8AY060epBjYK2Wy6F4Z2z34Y6Ai0o4uRdgDrpBucG58KGtTXO8aYZIPsBGvlMlLaLWMH0nWyH4mkR3KmQmltDAXyaa5MDCFeVwytjb7Z9VZrKkS8ET4RPhWwR4a21MNBqGWJeccF2phXwqdkbj9ViJhKtkTcwadMuPJlRUfEnStGeZ8M4eqofrbGJ4NruMiv7B-JoUKoRNztiU3WLr1w37Gonki6eoP7t139x6Cn5l8BAAD__zROhSY)**?**

The Solicitor General is the federal government’s lawyer at the Supreme Court. Today, that’s John Sauer. When one state sues another, the Justices often ask the Solicitor General to tell them where the federal government stands.

That means the Trump Administration’s voice could carry enormous weight in this case, and I intend to make sure his office hears from the Pro-Life Generation.

President Trump has said again and again that abortion should be decided by the states. **If that’s true, then the pro-life states deserve the federal government’s help protecting the laws their people passed.**

And right now, they aren’t getting enough of it.

The Justice Department is still on the other side of Louisiana in its separate lawsuit against the FDA over mail-order abortion pills.

That’s why the Solicitor General needs to hear from the Pro-Life Generation to make sure he understands what’s being shipped through the mail.

Louisiana’s attorney general had her own office order these pills online. They got them without speaking to a doctor, and nobody verified who they were. The bottles that arrived didn’t list the prescriber or a single risk.

Louisiana’s attorney general, Liz Murrill, put it plainly: _**“It is no different than if they were sending fentanyl in these boxes.”**_

And the attorney general is estimating that about 800 chemical abortions are committed every month in Louisiana, despite the state’s pro-life laws.

Nationwide, chemical abortion pills now account for more than two-thirds of all abortions, killing more than 600,000 preborn babies every year.

_And the women who take these deadly pills?_

A study from the _Ethics & Public Policy Center _recently found that nearly one in nine women suffers sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days of taking these pills. **That’s at least 22 times the rate printed on the drug’s own label!**

Now picture a teenage girl in Louisiana, alone with those pills, with no doctor who will ever see her and no name on the bottle to hold accountable . . .

Students for Life has been on the front lines of the fight against chemical abortion pills for years.

When Louisiana sued the FDA over mailing these pills into states where abortion is illegal, my team filed a legal brief in that case alongside more than a dozen other pro-life organizations.

Then, we put the FDA on notice for ignoring what chemical abortion pill waste is doing to our nation’s water and the endangered species that live in it.

And now, we’re preparing to file a legal brief in this shield law case, too. We’ve also done this before and seen the impact.

On the opening day of the Supreme Court’s term in October 2021, we carried more than half a million signed Moral Outcry Petitions up the marble steps of the Court. They were printed on two scrolls, each one 160 feet long, and it took a human chain of pro-lifers just to hold them up.
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckMuKhDAQRb8m7lryMuoii4HGXc92lpJOSi0wD5JoM38_OI8fmF3Bgbrn3o_H_DC4Y1jfjQdtT5xzmV8bZMBSN_Axmz0e1ebPmVOubozdmJyNrXjCLE3jtHVK8AY060epBjYK2Wy6F4Z2z34Y6Ai0o4uRdgDrpBucG58KGtTXO8aYZIPsBGvlMlLaLWMH0nWyH4mkR3KmQmltDAXyaa5MDCFeVwytjb7Z9VZrKkS8ET4RPhWwR4a21MNBqGWJeccF2phXwqdkbj9ViJhKtkTcwadMuPJlRUfEnStGeZ8M4eqofrbGJ4NruMiv7B-JoUKoRNztiU3WLr1w37Gonki6eoP7t139x6Cn5l8BAAD__zROhSY) _Roe v. Wade_ had been called “settled law” for 48 years.

Eight months later, it was gone.

I won’t tell you those scrolls ended Roe by themselves. **But I will tell you that pro-lifers who refuse to stay quiet have a way of changing what everyone else thinks is possible.**

This time, our team will be back on those steps with a legal brief in hand.

But I can’t get there on good intentions. Legal work costs money, and so does every campus stop where we tell students the TRUTH about these deadly pills.

[So please make your most generous tax-deductible contribution right now](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckMuKhDAQRb8m7lryMuoii4HGXc92lpJOSi0wD5JoM38_OI8fmF3Bgbrn3o_H_DC4Y1jfjQdtT5xzmV8bZMBSN_Axmz0e1ebPmVOubozdmJyNrXjCLE3jtHVK8AY060epBjYK2Wy6F4Z2z34Y6Ai0o4uRdgDrpBucG58KGtTXO8aYZIPsBGvlMlLaLWMH0nWyH4mkR3KmQmltDAXyaa5MDCFeVwytjb7Z9VZrKkS8ET4RPhWwR4a21MNBqGWJeccF2phXwqdkbj9ViJhKtkTcwadMuPJlRUfEnStGeZ8M4eqofrbGJ4NruMiv7B-JoUKoRNztiU3WLr1w37Gonki6eoP7t139x6Cn5l8BAAD__zROhSY)**:**
**> >> $25** puts pro-life materials in the hands of students at one campus stop.
**> >> $50** covers a tank of gas for a day of campus visits.
**> >> $100** launches a brand-new Students for Life group with flyers, postcards, and materials.
**> >> $250** helps put our team on a campus that has tried to keep us out.
**> >> $500** helps cover the security costs we now face at a single event.
Every dollar you give helps us expose chemical abortion pills, reach more students with the TRUTH, and keep fighting for every mother and baby these shield laws leave behind.
Governor Hochul defiantly said “not now, not ever.” I’d like to answer her with a legal brief at the Supreme Court, and I’d like you standing with me when we do.

Thank you for standing with me, and with every preborn baby in a state that chose to protect her.

For Life,

Kristan Hawkins
President, _Students for Life_

P.S. – Three pro-life states just asked the Supreme Court to strike down the shield laws protecting abortionists who mail chemical abortion pills across state lines. The federal government’s voice could make all the difference. We’re preparing a legal brief to stand with them, and I need your help to finish this fight. [Please give $500, $250, $100, $50, or $25 right away](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckMuKhDAQRb8m7lryMuoii4HGXc92lpJOSi0wD5JoM38_OI8fmF3Bgbrn3o_H_DC4Y1jfjQdtT5xzmV8bZMBSN_Axmz0e1ebPmVOubozdmJyNrXjCLE3jtHVK8AY060epBjYK2Wy6F4Z2z34Y6Ai0o4uRdgDrpBucG58KGtTXO8aYZIPsBGvlMlLaLWMH0nWyH4mkR3KmQmltDAXyaa5MDCFeVwytjb7Z9VZrKkS8ET4RPhWwR4a21MNBqGWJeccF2phXwqdkbj9ViJhKtkTcwadMuPJlRUfEnStGeZ8M4eqofrbGJ4NruMiv7B-JoUKoRNztiU3WLr1w37Gonki6eoP7t139x6Cn5l8BAAD__zROhSY)**.**
[GIVE NOW >>](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckMuKhDAQRb8m7lryMuoii4HGXc92lpJOSi0wD5JoM38_OI8fmF3Bgbrn3o_H_DC4Y1jfjQdtT5xzmV8bZMBSN_Axmz0e1ebPmVOubozdmJyNrXjCLE3jtHVK8AY060epBjYK2Wy6F4Z2z34Y6Ai0o4uRdgDrpBucG58KGtTXO8aYZIPsBGvlMlLaLWMH0nWyH4mkR3KmQmltDAXyaa5MDCFeVwytjb7Z9VZrKkS8ET4RPhWwR4a21MNBqGWJeccF2phXwqdkbj9ViJhKtkTcwadMuPJlRUfEnStGeZ8M4eqofrbGJ4NruMiv7B-JoUKoRNztiU3WLr1w37Gonki6eoP7t139x6Cn5l8BAAD__zROhSY)

On the opening day of the Supreme Court’s term in October 2021, we carried more than half a million signed Moral Outcry Petitions up the marble steps of the Court. They were printed on two scrolls, each one 160 feet long, and it took a human chain of pro-lifers just to hold them up. Roe v. Wade had been called “settled law” for 48 years. Eight months later, it was gone. I won’t tell you those scrolls ended Roe by themselves. But I will tell you that pro-lifers who refuse to stay quiet have a way of changing what everyone else thinks is possible. This time, our team will be back on those steps with a legal brief in hand. But I can’t get there on good intentions. Legal work costs money, and so does every campus stop where we tell students the TRUTH about these deadly pills. : >> $25 puts pro-life materials in the hands of students at one campus stop. >> $50 covers a tank of gas for a day of campus visits. >> $100 launches a brand-new Students for Life group with flyers, postcards, and materials. >> $250 helps put our team on a campus that has tried to keep us out. >> $500 helps cover the security costs we now face at a single event. Every dollar you give helps us expose chemical abortion pills, reach more students with the TRUTH, and keep fighting for every mother and baby these shield laws leave behind. Governor Hochul defiantly said “not now, not ever.” I’d like to answer her with a legal brief at the Supreme Court, and I’d like you standing with me when we do. Thank you for standing with me, and with every preborn baby in a state that chose to protect her. For Life, Kristan Hawkins President, Students for Life P.S. – Three pro-life states just asked the Supreme Court to strike down the shield laws protecting abortionists who mail chemical abortion pills across state lines. The federal government’s voice could make all the difference. **A MESSAGE FROM SHERIFF CHAD BIANCO**

My fellow Californians,
I’ve spent the past couple of weeks reflecting on the devastating loss we experienced on November 3rd.
We watched a hostile takeover of California by a ruling class in Sacramento that has long forgotten the people it serves. They have mastered the art of managing our state’s decline, leaving countless Californians believing their voices no longer matter.That must change.
When Sacramento locked down your churches and businesses, I said no. When cities burned in 2020, I kept Riverside County safe.When fentanyl began killing our children, we went after the cartels, seized millions of pills, and put criminals behind bars. I became the first in the nation to arrest a fentanyl supplier for murder.
When politicians threatened your Second Amendment rights, we issued a record numbers of concealed carry permits. And we did it all while balancing our budget.
**I’ve delivered on my promises. I’ve stood up when others backed down. I’ve challenged the powerful when others looked away.**
And I’m just getting started.I hope you’ll join me in this glorious and righteous fight for California.

Thank you, and God bless,
**Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County**

#### **The Greenback Returns**
## **A year after everyone wrote its obituary, the dollar hit a 19-month high**
_The strength of the dollar decides what your money buys, at home and abroad. This week it climbed to its highest level in well over a year._
A year ago, the fashionable take was that the dollar was finished. This week it climbed to a 19-month high instead.
---
The U.S. Dollar Index, which measures the greenback against six major currencies, touched about 102.9, a level last seen in April 2025. The spark was the force that has driven every market this week: a hot inflation reading and the near-certain prospect of a December rate hike. Higher American rates pull money from around the world into dollars.
It is quite a turn. In the first half of 2025 the dollar fell more than 10 percent, its worst start to a year since 1973, and plenty of people read that slide as proof that America was losing its financial crown.
A stronger dollar is a small raise for anyone who buys imported goods or plans a trip abroad, because each dollar now stretches further. The flip side is just as real. It squeezes U.S. companies that earn their money overseas, and it is part of why gold [slid toward 13-month lows](https://theeagledispatch.podia.com/p/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJuZXdzbGV0dGVyX2xpbmtfaWQiOjQ2MzQyMDB9.PTYk4YjVYYSv2vWY7fpfI-gA0KGtki88l6XjQ9tSLxM/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdHVkZW50X2lkIjo2NjAzOTM5OSwibmV3c2xldHRlcl9pZCI6MzMxNzg4OX0.Aq3WM0OlPwRuNC3NxDQkQ59SL0BkcEXFrAXRBNeQDks) this week, losing its shine against a currency that suddenly pays to hold.
The 10-year Treasury yield [topped 5 percent](https://theeagledispatch.podia.com/p/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJuZXdzbGV0dGVyX2xpbmtfaWQiOjQ2MzQyMDF9.Q1EwRvl-qVrY7DZzKVCq0e9DV8P-eN0n0hT7fC_a3-A/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdHVkZW50X2lkIjo2NjAzOTM5OSwibmV3c2xldHRlcl9pZCI6MzMxNzg4OX0.Aq3WM0OlPwRuNC3NxDQkQ59SL0BkcEXFrAXRBNeQDks) again, and I would not mistake this dollar strength for calm. It is the market bracing for the Fed to keep money expensive well into next year.
---
#### **The Scoreboard**
## **Stocks still won the week, even as Friday belonged to the bears**
Step back from one ugly session and the week looks better than it felt. All three major indexes finished higher, even as Friday sagged under a familiar weight.
---
▪ For the week, the S&P 500 rose about 2.5 percent, the Nasdaq about 2.3 percent, and the Dow about 2.1 percent, a solid run despite the nerves.
▪ Friday was the sour note. The Dow eked out a small gain while the S&P and Nasdaq slipped, as technology sold off and the rest of the market held firm.
▪ Nvidia stayed at the center of it. Its slide deepened after the chief executive's abrupt exit, and Wall Street turned cautious, with one analyst [cutting its rating](https://theeagledispatch.podia.com/p/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJuZXdzbGV0dGVyX2xpbmtfaWQiOjQ2MzQyMDJ9.U2mUFy5d77NMlhZcaxyJArIcMlVHZY4Vnu-XBk-0eJU/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdHVkZW50X2lkIjo2NjAzOTM5OSwibmV3c2xldHRlcl9pZCI6MzMxNzg4OX0.Aq3WM0OlPwRuNC3NxDQkQ59SL0BkcEXFrAXRBNeQDks) and warning the easy gains are over.
▪ The split is the story of the week: money stepped back from the crowded technology trade and spread into banks, energy and industrials, a healthier market than one leaning on a few names.
A green week with a red Friday is not a warning. It is the market doing what it should, letting leadership change hands instead of resting on the same giants.
---
#### **One Number**
**87%** is where futures markets now put the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike on December 9, [according to CME FedWatch](https://theeagledispatch.podia.com/p/l/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJuZXdzbGV0dGVyX2xpbmtfaWQiOjQ2MzQyMDN9.JTktLAVuxoHfu0qe32SnbKvhs9Do_8GR9PmK4OJi660/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdHVkZW50X2lkIjo2NjAzOTM5OSwibmV3c2xldHRlcl9pZCI6MzMxNzg4OX0.Aq3WM0OlPwRuNC3NxDQkQ59SL0BkcEXFrAXRBNeQDks). A month ago a cut was still on the table. Hotter inflation flipped the script, and a hike would push the Fed's benchmark to a range of 4 to 4.25 percent. For anyone carrying a credit-card balance or a variable-rate loan, that is the figure that quietly becomes a bigger minimum payment, right as the holiday bills arrive.
#### **Why I Led Here**
I led with the dollar because the loudest money story of the past two years has been its coming death, and this week it printed a 19-month high instead. I have heard the end of the dollar predicted more times than I can count, going back to my first years advising families, and it has outlived every forecast so far.
That is not flag-waving, it is pattern recognition. A currency backed by the deepest markets in the world and the habit of being everyone's reserve does not fade on a bad headline or even a bad year. It can weaken, and it did in 2025, yet betting on its funeral has been a losing trade for a very long time.

Peter, There are many stories to celebrate from last week’s election. One of my favorites: more doctors are joining me in Congress! I’ll tell you why this matters so much, but first let’s meet a few of them:

→ In the Senate, **Annie Andrews** , a pediatrician from South Carolina, will become the first pediatrician in the Senate, and **Abdul El-Sayed** , a physician and epidemiologist, will be the next senator from Michigan.

→ In the House, I’ll be joined by **Richard Pan** , a pediatrician from California; **Amish Shah** , an emergency medical doctor from Arizona; and **Adam Hamaway** , a surgeon from New Jersey.

Here’s why their arrival in Congress matters so much right now:

**They can push back on disinformation.** Our Health Secretary has a long record of anti-vaccine activism and has downplayed the measles outbreaks spreading across the country. We need actual doctors and health professionals who can call out that disinformation with the credibility that comes from years of caring for patients and our public health.

**They bring real-world experience.** Physicians know firsthand how healthcare policies affect patients. That experience helps them understand and explain policies that affect millions of Americans, write legislation that will improve our health system, and fund the programs that keep the public healthy.

**They will put healthcare front and center.** They ran on improving our healthcare system at a time when families are facing higher premiums, higher deductibles, and higher drug costs that make it harder to get ahead. These health experts will be focused on making life better for all Americans, just like the communities they’ve served.

**They will focus on results.** Many of these physicians won in districts that went to Trump in 2024, which tells me that voters across the political spectrum care about results – they want elected officials who will bring their healthcare costs down and make decisions based on evidence.

And we need that leadership now more than ever. Last year, Republicans made the largest cuts to healthcare in our nation’s history, throwing more than 10 million people off Medicaid and spiking premiums for many millions more. All to bankroll $4.5 trillion in tax cuts that overwhelmingly benefitted billionaires and massive corporations. The bill’s most brutal impacts take effect next year, and right here in Minnesota, we’re facing _double-digit increases_ in our health insurance premiums.

Expertise alone won’t save us, but we’ve seen what happens when ideology overrides science, and we deserve leaders we can trust to make good public health decisions.

**I care deeply about public health – as a physician, and as a human. I will never stop fighting for your right to access safe, science-backed health care, and I’m glad to have some new colleagues in the fight with me.**

Thank you for standing with us, and for your support.

With gratitude and resolve,
Kelly

The Benson trailer sat on the shoulder of Interstate 94 West with its rear doors open. A state trooper and a USDOT officer walked the length of it -- floor, straps, doors, the paperwork on the driver's clipboard. Press photos from the last week of July show the same tableau repeated across four states: a white Peterbilt waved into a checkpoint lane by an Indiana trooper on I-94; Iowa patrolmen directing a yellow Kenworth and a white Freightliner under a hard late-July sun.
What looked like a routine DOT check was not. From July 28 through 30, 2026, inspectors from the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration worked alongside ICE's Homeland Security Investigations and the state highway patrols of Illinois, Indiana, Iowa and Ohio in a pre-planned sweep the agencies named Operation Highway Shield -- the second wave of an operation that debuted in Florida in March. Per USDOT's own behind-the-scenes posts, the detail focused on semi-trucks tailgating through active work zones, and on the documents behind the driver: license class, immigration status, and whether he could read an English road sign.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7c5363c6-a4c8-4374-a59b-1b76f7e4d8d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Seventy-two hours produced 3,487 enforcement stops. Out of those came 766 drivers and vehicles placed out of service -- the government never published the split between trucks and drivers, only the combined figure. Thirty-six violations for failing English Language Proficiency tests. Fifty-one people detained on immigration violations, twenty-one of them behind the wheel on non-domiciled commercial licenses issued by California and New York -- permits minted a continent away from the shoulder where their holders were stopped. Eighty-six operators arrested for what the government summarizes as dangerous behavior: road rage, domestic violence, the ordinary felonies roadside work trips over. And the cargo -- nearly $1 million in stolen freight recovered across three cargo-theft investigations, trailers that were somebody's inventory until troopers happened to be looking...

In January, Democrats will have new majorities in the House and Senate.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=4126%2E21716%2EnscFBB)
In January, Democrats will have new majorities in the House and Senate. Here’s what’s on my to do list:
1. **Lower the cost of living.** All throughout this campaign, families across Delaware told me the same thing: everything costs too much. Groceries, rent, childcare, prescriptions. Congress needs to act on that immediately, and I’m going to make sure we do.

2. **Hold Trump’s corrupt administration accountable.** For too long, no one in Washington has been checking this administration’s power. As a result, corruption has run rampant — and it’s costing American taxpayers. We need to use every oversight tool we have to shine a light on what’s happening and hold those responsible accountable.

3. **Protect and expand access to healthcare.** No one should go without care because of what’s in their bank account. But when Republicans passed Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill” in the last Congress, they ripped health insurance away from millions. We need to not only reverse the damage Republicans have done, but do even more to make healthcare more accessible to working families across Delaware and the country.

This is the work voters elected us to do, and I intend to start the moment we’re sworn in. But I’m counting on your support every step of the way.

This is Rep. Patricia “Pat” Moore (D-LA).
Last week, Democrats won big. The House. The Senate. Seats in places nobody thought we could win.
But right now, the political world is asking one question: Was that the start of something, or a flash in the pan?
The answer won’t come from the pundits. It will come from the next races on the board, and the very first is my race.
_**On December 12, Louisiana’s 5th Congressional District goes to a runoff. I finished first. Now I have to finish the job.**_
History tells us exactly what’s at stake.
In 2008, Democrats rode a historic wave. Less than a month later, in a Georgia Senate runoff, our turnout dropped off and Republicans held the seat. A year after that, Republicans flipped Ted Kennedy’s old Senate seat in Massachusetts, and the far right came roaring back to take the House in 2010.
The lesson is simple: The moment we show weakness, they come roaring back.
If we win here we send a message to the entire country: Tuesday wasn’t the exception. It was the rule.

body:
In our family, every single day is a Diabetes Day!

| | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143465050/660297557/297443936?refcode=BLU_EM_SSFC_2026-11-14_02&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTgxNzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiODc0Yjg2NGMtNjllMC1mMTExLTkxZjAtMDAwZDNhMThlMjQ0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2PM9IWpNPomhWaHtkMiI1gWg5hWi8AP08gA-ELMlKws=)
---
| | | November is Diabetes Awareness Month and today is World Diabetes Day. In our family, every day became a day impacted by type one diabetes after our daughter, Elle, was diagnosed over Thanksgiving nearly 19 years ago.
---
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143465051/660297558/297443936?refcode=BLU_EM_SSFC_2026-11-14_02&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTgxNzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiODc0Yjg2NGMtNjllMC1mMTExLTkxZjAtMDAwZDNhMThlMjQ0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2PM9IWpNPomhWaHtkMiI1gWg5hWi8AP08gA-ELMlKws=)
---
| | In the early years following her diagnosis, Elle was pricking her fingers 10-12 times and taking 8-10 shots of insulin every single day. Today, thanks to medical research, Elle wears an insulin pump on one arm and a continuous glucose monitor on the other. We know that progress is possible, but it requires a commitment to science and medical research. Most importantly, it requires that people can get access to health care and treatment when and where they need it!
---
Millions of Americans live with diabetes, and many more care for someone who does. This disease is relentless and dangerous. No one should ever be forced to ration insulin needed to stay alive.
This month marks the start of my service as a newly elected member of Congress. I am humbled by this immense responsibility and will carry my understanding of the challenges facing people living with diabetes and other chronic diseases with me every single day. I know that our healthcare system is broken, making care for far too many people inaccessible and unaffordable. In honor of World Diabetes Day, I renew my commitment to fight to fix our broken healthcare system.
Thank you for being a part of our fight for people with diabetes and for all those with chronic illnesses.
And to my daughter Elle, who provides endless motivation and inspiration — I love you MORE!
Onward,
Stefany

clean_body: In our family, every single day is a Diabetes Day! | | | | = | | | November is Diabetes Awareness Month and today is World Diabetes Day. In our family, every day became a day impacted by type one diabetes after our daughter, Elle, was diagnosed over Thanksgiving nearly 19 years ago. | | | = | | In the early years following her diagnosis, Elle was pricking her fingers 10-12 times and taking 8-10 shots of insulin every single day. Today, thanks to medical research, Elle wears an insulin pump on one arm and a continuous glucose monitor on the other. We know that progress is possible, but it requires a commitment to science and medical research. Most importantly, it requires that people can get access to health care and treatment when and where they need it! Millions of Americans live with diabetes, and many more care for someone who does. This disease is relentless and dangerous. No one should ever be forced to ration insulin needed to stay alive. This month marks the start of my service as a newly elected member of Congress. I am humbled by this immense responsibility and will carry my understanding of the challenges facing people living with diabetes and other chronic diseases with me every single day. I know that our healthcare system is broken, making care for far too many people inaccessible and unaffordable. In honor of World Diabetes Day, I renew my commitment to fight to fix our broken healthcare system. Thank you for being a part of our fight for people with diabetes and for all those with chronic illnesses. And to my daughter Elle, who provides endless motivation and inspiration — I love you MORE! Onward, Stefany | | | | = | | | | | | = | | | | | | Paid for by Stefany Shaheen for Congress | | Stefany Shaheen for Congress PO Box 193 Manchester, NH 03105 United States | | | | = | | | = | | This message was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. | |

subject: First Week in Washington, Laubacher Pushes to Deliver on Campaign Promise to Ban Congressional Stock Trading
body:
Laubacher turns campaign promise into action, pushing House leadership to ban congressional stock trading on Day One.

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ZPDalP6f9s1?e=1c5f08419c&c2id=9f711ebcee4618a2092828a4c98e410a)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE****Date:** November 14, 2026 **Contact:**[ Taylor Gillespie](mailto:info@eileenforcolorado.com?subject=&body=), 720-557-6185
---
| | **First Week in Washington, Laubacher Pushes to Deliver on Campaign Promise to Ban Congressional Stock Trading** _Laubacher turns campaign promise into action, pushing House leadership to ban congressional stock trading on Day One._
---
| |
**WASHINGTON, D.C. —** This week, in her first official action as a member-elect, Eileen Laubacher joined 50 other incoming members of Congress in a letter calling on House Democratic leadership to adopt a ban on stock trading in the House rules package on the first day of the new Congress. The proposed rule would prevent members of Congress and their spouses from buying or selling individual stocks, commodities, futures, derivatives and related investments.
“Members of Congress shouldn’t be trading stocks in the very industries they’re supposed to oversee while hardworking Americans struggle to afford groceries and rent,” said **Congresswoman-elect Eileen Laubacher.** “I promised the people of Colorado’s 4th District I’d fight to clean up Washington. I’m not waiting until I’m sworn in to get started. House leadership should make banning congressional stock trading a priority on day one.”
The full text of the letter can be read below:
_Members of Congress are getting rich trading stock in the industries they regulate while the people they represent fall behind on rent and groceries. Voters sent a message last Tuesday loudly and clearly: they want lower costs and an end to corrupt self-dealing. Democrats can deliver both starting the day the new Congress is sworn in. _
_We are calling on our Democratic leaders in the House to quickly adopt a rule barring members and their_ _spouses from owning or trading stocks, commodities, futures, derivatives, and other related securities, with limited exceptions such as a diversified mutual fund or an investment held in a qualified blind trust. Democrats may have won the election, but we have a long way to go to earn back the trust of voters across the country. The existing laws around insider trading are insufficient. We should hold ourselves to the highest standard and work to restore faith in government. Nobody should leave Congress with millions more in their bank accounts. _
_A stock trading ban alone will not fix Washington, but it is the fastest way to show voters we heard them. This rule would be a down payment on much-needed reform to prevent elected and appointed government officials and their spouses from trading stocks. We promised our communities we would clean up this place. In January, we should do just that. _**###**

Karoline Leavitt may be from New Hampshire, but she does not represent the values that make our state great.

Granite Staters believe in integrity, accountability, and the responsibility that comes with serving the American people. We expect our elected officials and public servants to tell the truth, put Americans first, and stand up for what’s right. _That’s the exact opposite of everything she’s done._

While Karoline Leavitt spends her time defending Donald Trump and his administration, Maggie Hassan is fighting to protect access to health care, hold this administration accountable, and deliver real results for New Hampshire families.

Take a look at three EMILYs List U.S. House candidates who ran multiple times and flipped key seats in this year’s blue wave:
**Christina Bohannan (IA-01):** Christina ran against Republican Mariannette Miller-Meeks in both 2022 and 2024. In her 2024 race, she came within just 0.2% of defeating Miller-Meeks. With this close of a defeat last cycle, we knew that Christina had a real shot to win this year. Sure enough, she won decisively with a 9.6% advantage over Miller-Meeks.
**Janelle Stelson (PA-10):** Janelle Stelson ran against Scott Perry in 2024, and she lost by just 1.2%. Perry had held this seat since 2013, but make no mistake: He was one of our most vulnerable opponents this cycle. This year, Janelle delivered Perry a staggering defeat, winning this critical Mission Majority race by 10.4%.
**Rebecca Cooke (WI-03):** Republican Derrick Van Orden beat Rebecca Cooke by just 2.8% in 2024. Van Orden has made a name for himself as one of the most extreme members of Congress, and voters were clearly tired of his corruption. This year, Rebecca beat him by 6.6%.
Just because a candidate doesn’t win on the first try doesn’t mean she’s not viable. Breaking Republican strongholds doesn’t happen overnight. Women like Christina, Janelle, and Rebecca are proof that when you continue to invest in the right candidates and lay the groundwork, **change is possible.**
This is why the work we do is so important. But now it’s up to us to make sure these women hold these highly competitive seats.
Scott Perry and Derrick Van Orden have both already filed to try and win back their old seats in 2028. With Republican megadonors in their pocket, we can be sure they’re going to come back with a vengeance.

clean_body: Breaking Republican strongholds doesn’t happen overnight. | = Peter, Recruiting, training, and investing in Democratic pro-choice women candidates is a winning strategy — even if they don’t win on the first try. = | = Take a look at three EMILYs List U.S. House candidates who ran multiple times and flipped key seats in this year’s blue wave: Christina Bohannan (IA-01): Christina ran against Republican Mariannette Miller-Meeks in both 2022 and 2024. In her 2024 race, she came within just 0.2% of defeating Miller-Meeks. With this close of a defeat last cycle, we knew that Christina had a real shot to win this year. Sure enough, she won decisively with a 9.6% advantage over Miller-Meeks. Janelle Stelson (PA-10): Janelle Stelson ran against Scott Perry in 2024, and she lost by just 1.2%. Perry had held this seat since 2013, but make no mistake: He was one of our most vulnerable opponents this cycle. This year, Janelle delivered Perry a staggering defeat, winning this critical Mission Majority race by 10.4%. Rebecca Cooke (WI-03): Republican Derrick Van Orden beat Rebecca Cooke by just 2.8% in 2024. Van Orden has made a name for himself as one of the most extreme members of Congress, and voters were clearly tired of his corruption. This year, Rebecca beat him by 6.6%. Just because a candidate doesn’t win on the first try doesn’t mean she’s not viable. Breaking Republican strongholds doesn’t happen overnight. Women like Christina, Janelle, and Rebecca are proof that when you continue to invest in the right candidates and lay the groundwork, change is possible. This is why the work we do is so important. But now it’s up to us to make sure these women hold these highly competitive seats. Scott Perry and Derrick Van Orden have both already filed to try and win back their old seats in 2028.
